title: Make apps/api database layer engine-agnostic (Postgres + SQLite)
description: Replace the hard-wired pg.Pool/raw-SQL data layer (23 files, ~125 call sites) with a Kysely-based typed SQL layer supporting both PostgreSQL and SQLite, so the app no longer requires a standalone Postgres install for local dev/small self-hosted use. See plan at /home/jmuir/.claude/plans/we-need-to-make-graceful-ocean.md for full rationale, approach comparison, and phase breakdown. Scope: Postgres + SQLite only (no MySQL). SQLite documented as dev/small-deployment only (concurrency caveat), Azure prod deployment stays Postgres by default. Reverses/amends Constitution VI's 'no ORM' stance via an explicit amendment (Kysely is a typed SQL compiler, not an ORM).
acceptance_criteria: apps/api contract test suite passes against both Postgres and SQLite (TEST_DB_CLIENT env var); a cold install with DB_CLIENT=sqlite and no Docker/Postgres running completes the README quickstart; docs/constitution updated to reflect the new data-access approach.

title: Container-role + parentContainerId authoring infrastructure (foundational)
description:
Single highest-leverage fix in the whole visual-authoring-parity roadmap. AddContainerInput (packages/diagram-core/src/model/diagram-ops.ts:330-334) has no role field, and no op sets DiagramContainer.parentContainerId at all. Canvas.tsx's two container-creation call sites (Canvas.tsx:1027, :1277) and the AI's groupIntoContainer tool (apps/api/src/ai/diagram-tools.ts:412-436) can therefore only ever produce a plain, role-less, unnested container. Blocks: sequence loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect/box/note-left/note-right/note-over, UML namespace/note, and C4 boundary-kind selection.

Work: (1) diagram-ops.ts -- add role?/parentContainerId? to AddContainerInput, plus a new setContainerRole(model, containerId, role) op (mirrors the existing updateNodeRole pattern, diagram-ops.ts:191-201) and a setContainerParent/assignContainerToContainer op (mirrors assignNodeToContainer, diagram-ops.ts:420-429). (2) diagram-tools.ts -- extend groupIntoContainer with a family-conditional kind/role parameter, following the existing per-family tool-availability pattern (createDiagramTools(context, family) already gates setNodeRole/setEntityAttributes per family). (3) Canvas UI -- extend the Add Container flow with a role-select step gated by dslFamily (loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect/box/note-left/note-right/note-over for sequence; namespace/note for uml; the 5 boundary kinds from canvas-7vs.11's BOUNDARY_KEYWORD_TO_ROLE map for c4), plus a small post-creation kind affordance mirroring the existing renderFieldsAffordance/renderStylePopup foreignObject-popup pattern (Canvas.tsx:1164-1250). Sequence's ranged blocks (loop/alt/...) span a range of messages, not a point-in-time like activate/deactivate -- reuse the existing multi-select + groupSelected mechanism (Canvas.tsx:1277), extended to also set sequenceOrder bounds from the selected messages' own order, rather than inventing a new interaction model.
acceptance_criteria: A user can visually create a role-typed, correctly-family-scoped container (sequence block/note/box, UML namespace/note, C4 boundary) via the canvas UI, and it round-trips through the DSL correctly. groupIntoContainer AI tool gains matching role parameter. New Playwright e2e coverage.
close_reason: Delivered: (1) diagram-ops.ts gained role/parentContainerId/attachedNodeIds/sequenceOrder on AddContainerInput, plus setContainerRole, setContainerParent/removeContainerParent, and assignEdgeToContainer/removeEdgeFromContainer (new sequence-message-membership ops) -- removeContainer also fixed to release member edges, a real dangling-reference gap this bead's new edge-membership concept would otherwise have introduced. (2) diagram-tools.ts's groupIntoContainer gained a family-conditional kind parameter (CONTAINER_ROLE_OPTIONS: c4's 5 boundary kinds via a newly-exported C4_BOUNDARY_ROLES single-source-of-truth in dsl/c4.ts, uml's namespace/note, sequence's box) -- also had to update diagram-type-primers.ts's c4/uml prose to keep the FR-005 anti-drift guard green. (3) Canvas.tsx: a family-scoped 'Container Kind' picker next to Add Container/Group into Container, wired through both handlers. Delivers real, working visual creation of UML namespace+standalone note, all 5 C4 boundary kinds, and sequence box groupings -- all round-trip through the DSL. Deliberately deferred to canvas-2s6.2 (descriptions updated accordingly): sequence's RANGED control-flow blocks (loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect), since they enclose a range of MESSAGES not the node-based membership this bead's reused Group-into-Container gesture grants -- needs a new multi-edge-select mechanism (selectedEdgeId is deliberately single-select today) or equivalent; and sequence's note-left/right/over (point-in-time, participant-attached, need a different creation gesture than multi-node select). UML 'note' is intentionally NOT reachable via Group into Container (disabled when Kind=Note) since notes attach via attachedNodeIds not containerId membership -- reachable via plain Add Container + the existing container-rename affordance instead, a disclosed narrower scope. 115+52 new/updated unit tests (diagram-ops.test.ts, diagram-tools.test.ts), 8 new Playwright e2e cases (container-role-authoring.spec.ts) plus a 50-test regression subset (containers/multi-select/fields-affordance/erd-cardinality/entity-rendering/import/sequence-rendering) all green. Full suites: diagram-core 764/764, apps/api 322/322+1 skip, apps/web tsc clean, eslint clean across every touched file.

title: ER relationship cardinality (crow's-foot notation) parsed but discarded — renders as generic arrow instead
description: Reported live: 'the diagram is rendering arrows and it should be rendering crows feet notation'. Root cause is worse than a rendering gap (unlike canvas-x66's attributes/members bug, where the data WAS in the model) -- the DiagramEdge model has NO field for ER cardinality at all. packages/diagram-core/src/dsl/erd.ts's own doc comment on parseErd already discloses this: 'Any cardinality notation (||--o{, ||--||, etc.) parses correctly, but ... DiagramEdge has no cardinality field, so serialization always emits the common one-to-many token (||--o{).' Confirmed in code: RELATIONSHIP_PATTERN's regex DOES capture the full cardinality+line token (e.g. '||--o{') as its 2nd capture group, but erd.ts:206's destructuring (const [, source, , target, label] = relMatch;) explicitly SKIPS that capture group -- the real cardinality is read off the line and then immediately thrown away, every time, for every relationship, regardless of what was actually typed. edges.push() never sets any cardinality field, so / stay undefined, and svg-renderer.ts's renderEdge (line ~541) falls through to its default: a plain 'marker-end="url(#arrowhead)")' triangular arrowhead, identical to any other diagram family's edge. This is a real data-integrity bug on top of the missing visual: reopening/re-exporting ANY erDiagram silently corrupts every relationship's actual specified cardinality to the generic one-to-many default (e.g. CUSTOMER ||--|| ORDER, an exactly-one-to-exactly-one relationship, silently becomes CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER on save) -- this violates FR-003 (no element silently dropped/altered), and there is an existing test (packages/diagram-core/tests/contract/erd-attributes.test.ts's 'cardinality normalization (documented limitation)' describe block) that currently locks in and asserts this exact lossy behavior as correct -- it will need rewriting once fixed.
acceptance_criteria: DiagramEdge gains erSourceCardinality/erTargetCardinality fields (raw 2-character token stored verbatim as it appears in the DSL, e.g. '||', 'o|', 'o{', '|{' -- not normalized to an enum, so each of the two characters can be rendered independently as its own glyph). The existing lineStyle field's 'dotted' value is reused for a non-identifying (..) relationship rather than adding a redundant new boolean. Parser captures and stores the real token instead of discarding it; serializer round-trips the real token (falling back to the current ||--o{ default only for an edge with neither field set, e.g. one added via the canvas UI's plain 'add edge' action rather than imported from DSL). Both renderers draw real crow's-foot glyphs (perpendicular tick = '|'/one, hollow circle = 'o'/zero-optional, three-pronged fork = '{'/'}'/many) at each endpoint instead of the generic plain arrowhead, sharing one geometry calculation (mirrors the tableNodeLayout/clipEdgeEndpoint shared-geometry precedent already established in svg-renderer.ts, so canvas and export stay pixel-identical per this codebase's SC-004 convention).
notes: An edge with neither erSourceCardinality nor erTargetCardinality set (every non-ERD edge, or an ERD edge added directly via canvas UI with no DSL round-trip yet) keeps today's plain-arrowhead rendering exactly -- no regression to the other five families.
close_reason: Fixed: DiagramEdge gained erSourceCardinality/erTargetCardinality (raw crow's-foot tokens). Parser now captures them instead of discarding; serializer round-trips the real value instead of normalizing to the default one-to-many token. Both renderers draw real crow's-foot glyphs (tick/circle/fork) via a shared cardinalityGlyphs() geometry function, replacing the generic arrowhead for ER edges. Verified live against the reported DSL. 558/558 diagram-core tests passing (12 new), 3/3 new e2e tests passing.

title: Sequence diagrams have no lifeline/timeline layout or rendering at all
acceptance_criteria: Not fully specified here -- this is sized like a real feature (spec-kit worthy per this repo's own constitution, not a quick bug fix): participants get real vertical lifelines; messages are ordered top-to-bottom by declaration order (not left-to-right in one row); activate/deactivate render as an activation bar segment on the relevant lifeline; loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break render as a bounding box around the message span they contain, with role-appropriate labeling; notes and box groupings render distinctly from a generic dashed rectangle. Whoever picks this up should scope/spec it properly rather than treat it as a drop-in fix -- likely needs its own specs/NNN-... entry per this repo's established process for changes of this size.

title: SSO login completed but session never recognized: /auth/me and /auth/logout gated behind allowLocalAuth
description: Live-verified against the deployed Azure instance (canvas-api + canvas-keycloak): clicking 'Sign in with SSO' DID work end-to-end at the network level -- /auth/login redirects to Keycloak via the /idp/* reverse proxy, the Keycloak login page and its assets render correctly (all confirmed via curl and a real headless-Chromium Playwright run). But GET /auth/me and POST /auth/logout lived inside auth/local.ts's registerLocalAuthRoutes, gated behind config.allowLocalAuth (app.ts:69-71) -- which the Azure deployment deliberately defaults to false (canvas-ycu.1, SSO-only). So App.tsx's on-load session check (GET /auth/me, called unconditionally on every page load) 404'd every single time, including immediately after a real, successful OIDC callback that had already set request.session.user. The frontend caught the 404, called setUser(null), and the user landed right back on the login screen with zero indication anything had happened -- exactly the 'when clicked nothing happens' symptom reported. Root cause confirmed live: curl to https://canvas-api.../auth/me returned 404 on the deployed instance before any fix.
acceptance_criteria: GET /auth/me and POST /auth/logout are registered unconditionally (moved to a new registerSessionInfoRoutes in auth/session.ts, called from app.ts regardless of config.allowLocalAuth); POST /auth/local/login stays gated. New contract test (tests/contract/session-info-routes.test.ts) builds the app with allowLocalAuth:false and asserts /auth/me returns 401 (not 404) and /auth/logout returns 204 (not 404), while /auth/local/login still 404s. Full apps/api vitest suite passes (257/257).
notes: Existing e2e sso-login.spec.ts (E2E_SSO_READY gated, not run in CI) would also have exercised this path, but only against local dev where .env sets ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH=true -- so even that test could never have caught the Azure-specific allowLocalAuth:false default. tests/helpers/setup.ts forces allowLocalAuth:true for every other contract test too, which is why this was invisible to the whole existing suite until tested against the real deployment.
close_reason: Fixed: /auth/me and /auth/logout moved to a new unconditionally-registered registerSessionInfoRoutes (session.ts), no longer gated behind allowLocalAuth. New contract test session-info-routes.test.ts. Deployed live to canvas-api (revision canvas-api--0000003) and the frontend static site; live-verified GET /auth/me now returns 401 (was 404) and POST /auth/logout returns 204 (was 404) on the real Azure deployment.

title: Fix Azure deployment bugs found during first live deploy: idp-proxy JSON forwarding, Postgres password URL-safety, duplicate AcrPull role assignment
description: Found live during the first-ever real deploy of infra/azure/ and the resulting SSO login attempt. Three real bugs fixed: (1) apps/api/src/auth/idp-proxy.routes.ts -- Fastify's built-in application/json content-type parser always takes precedence over a '*' wildcard parser regardless of registration order, so every JSON-bodied request forwarded through the /idp proxy (every Keycloak admin-API write) was silently mangled into the literal string '[object Object]' before reaching Keycloak, which rejected it with a generic 'Cannot parse the JSON' -- this is what made the user's SSO login fail with 'Invalid parameter: redirect_uri' un-fixable via the normal reconciliation path. Fixed with removeAllContentTypeParsers() first. (2) infra/azure/deploy.sh's Postgres admin password generation (openssl rand -base64 24) could produce +/=/ characters that broke DATABASE_URL's strict URL parsing -- filtered to alphanumeric-only. (3) apiapp.bicep and keycloak.bicep both declared a redundant AcrPull role assignment for the same identity, causing RoleAssignmentExists on redeploy -- removed the duplicate. NOT fixed in this pass, filed as follow-up: deploy.sh's own Keycloak client-reconciliation step uses grant_type=password direct-grant against Keycloak's master-realm admin, but Keycloak 25+/26's KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD-created admin is temporary and direct-grant rejects it outright -- only the browser Authorization Code flow (PKCE) works, confirmed live. This is why deploy.sh always silently skips reconciliation and a fresh deploy's realm keeps the localhost:3000 dev placeholder until patched by hand.
design: See CLAUDE.md's own Recent Changes entry for the full writeup of each bug, root cause, and fix. The unfixed reconciliation-login bug should eventually be fixed by having deploy.sh perform the same PKCE Authorization Code flow (fetch login page for a code_challenge/session_code, POST credentials to the login-actions URL, exchange the returned code for a token) instead of grant_type=password, mirroring the manual workaround already proven to work this session.
acceptance_criteria: All three fixes verified live against the actual deployed environment (redeployed, migrations succeeded, SSO login flow confirmed working end-to-end through to Keycloak's CONFIGURE_TOTP step). New regression test added in idp-proxy.test.ts for the JSON-forwarding bug specifically.
close_reason: All three of this bead's own fixes shipped and were live-verified in PR #84 (idp-proxy JSON forwarding, Postgres password URL-safety, duplicate AcrPull role assignment) -- it was left open purely pending its one child, canvas-0x7.1 (Keycloak PKCE reconciliation), now also closed via PR #99.

title: Proper Azure installation: Bicep IaC (private VNet/Postgres/Key Vault/Container Apps) with pause/resume/destroy lifecycle scripts
description:
docs/azure-deployment.md's own header calls it "a minimal, no-Dockerfile path... a demo/
throwaway-friendly path, not a hardened production topology" -- and it's accurate: hand-run az
CLI commands with no IaC at all, Postgres opened with --public-access 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255
(the entire internet, gated only by password), no Key Vault (secrets passed as plain App Service
app settings), no managed identity, no VNet, and no lifecycle management beyond a single
`az group delete` teardown. This bead is to replace that with a real, reproducible,
properly-secured deployment.

/home/jmuir/projects/ADP (different stack, same Azure target) already has exactly this, proven in
production: infra/azure/ is a complete Bicep IaC stack + a deploy/pause/resume/destroy script
suite. Read it in full before starting -- it is the reference to mimic, not just inspire from.

ADP's resource topology (infra/azure/main.bicep, subscription-scope, one resource group, modules
in infra/azure/modules/):
- acr.bicep -- Container Registry, admin user DISABLED (adminUserEnabled: false); images pulled
  via the API app's managed identity's AcrPull role, never a shared admin credential.
- network.bicep -- one VNet, two delegated subnets (Postgres, Container Apps env) + a private DNS
  zone, so Postgres has NO public endpoint at all -- the opposite of the current canvas doc's
  wide-open approach.
- postgres.bicep -- Flexible Server, VNet-integrated/private, Burstable Standard_B1ms, 32GB
  (cheapest viable tier -- matches what canvas's own doc already uses, just made private).
- keyvault.bicep -- Key Vault (RBAC-authorized, not legacy access policies) + a user-assigned
  managed identity. The identity gets the built-in "Key Vault Secrets User" role; the deploying
  principal gets "Key Vault Secrets Officer" so the deploy script can write secret VALUES
  imperatively afterward (`az keyvault secret set`) -- no secret value ever appears in the Bicep
  template or a deployment parameter. Purge protection deliberately OFF, specifically so destroy
  can fully remove the vault instead of leaving it soft-deleted-but-name-reserved.
- containerappsenv.bicep -- one VNet-integrated Container Apps environment hosting every app
  (Log Analytics-backed logging).
- apiapp.bicep -- the public-facing app. minReplicas=0/maxReplicas=1 (scale-to-zero when idle --
  a real cost saving since a Node/uvicorn-class cold start is seconds, not disruptive).
- migrationjob.bicep -- a manual-trigger Container Apps Job running the same image as the API app
  with a different command (DB migrations), rather than migrating on container boot.

Lifecycle scripts (infra/azure/{deploy,pause,resume,destroy}.sh) -- THE PART THIS BEAD MUST
MIMIC AS CLOSELY AS POSSIBLE, per explicit instruction:
- deploy.sh: generates+caches admin passwords locally (gitignored infra/azure/.secrets/, chmod
  600) on first run so re-deploys don't rotate credentials out from under a running server;
  pre-seeds Key Vault secret VALUES before the main deployment (container apps reference them by
  name at provisioning time, so they must already exist); builds+pushes the image tagged with the
  git short SHA -- NOT a floating `:latest`, which Container Apps' revision diffing treats as a
  no-op even when the underlying digest changed (a real bug they hit); runs `az deployment sub
  what-if` and requires an explicit y/N confirmation before applying.
- pause.sh: stops Postgres compute only (`az postgres flexible-server stop`, storage/data
  retained) and drops container app(s) to minReplicas=0 (Container Apps rejects maxReplicas=0
  outright, so "paused" means "eligible to scale to zero", not instant/forced). Documents what
  STILL costs money while paused (storage, ACR image storage, Key Vault ops -- all small) and the
  real gotcha that Azure auto-restarts a stopped Postgres Flexible Server after 7 days if not
  resumed manually.
- resume.sh: reverses pause.sh exactly -- starts Postgres, restores each container app's normal
  scale settings (not identical for every app -- match whatever each app's own steady-state
  scale actually is), then polls `az postgres flexible-server show --query state` until `Ready`
  rather than assuming instant availability.
- destroy.sh: requires typing the resource group name to confirm (not just y/N -- a full-data-
  loss action deserves a stronger confirmation than pause/resume do); deletes the resource group
  with `--no-wait` + explicit polling (a VNet-integrated Container Apps environment reliably takes
  15+ minutes to delete, long enough to hit foreground command timeouts); THEN separately purges
  the soft-deleted Key Vault (plain `az group delete` only soft-deletes it -- the name stays
  reserved, blocking the next deploy with "vault already exists in deleted state" -- unless
  explicitly purged), falling back to scanning the subscription's soft-deleted-vaults list by
  name prefix if the resource group was already gone before this ran (so it still recovers from
  a manual/partial teardown). Deliberately leaves the local cached .secrets/ alone so a future
  rebuild reuses the same credentials.

Real gotchas documented in ADP's own comments, worth carrying over rather than rediscovering:
- First-ever deploy is a two-pass bootstrap: Key Vault doesn't exist yet, so secrets can't be
  pre-seeded, so any module referencing them by name fails on run 1 -- expected, re-run once Key
  Vault exists.
- The public URL a browser reaches an internal-ingress service through (if canvas's own Keycloak
  integration, canvas-mi9, ends up needing the same internal-Container-App + reverse-proxy
  pattern ADP uses) has to be constructed from the environment's stable default domain, not the
  app's own output FQDN, to avoid a circular dependency between the two modules needing each
  other's address.
acceptance_criteria:
- A version-controlled IaC template (Bicep, mirroring ADP's module structure) deploys canvas's
  full stack into one resource group from a single entry point -- not hand-run az CLI steps.
- Postgres is VNet-integrated with NO public network access, replacing the current doc's
  --public-access 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255.
- All secrets (DB connection string, SESSION_SECRET, etc.) live in Key Vault, referenced via a
  user-assigned managed identity -- never a plain app setting or committed value.
- pause.sh / resume.sh / destroy.sh exist and behave like ADP's: pause stops Postgres compute +
  drops compute to scale-to-zero-eligible while retaining all data; resume reverses it and polls
  Postgres for Ready before declaring success; destroy requires typing the resource group name to
  confirm, deletes the RG, and separately purges the Key Vault (since a plain RG delete only
  soft-deletes it and would block the next deploy under the same name).
- A single deploy script mirrors deploy.sh: cached local secrets (gitignored) so re-deploys don't
  rotate credentials, git-sha image tagging (not floating :latest), a what-if dry run, and an
  explicit confirmation before applying.
- docs/azure-deployment.md is replaced or clearly marked superseded -- not left in place
  contradicting the new path (the current doc should either become "quick throwaway demo only,
  see X for the real deployment" or be removed).
notes: Implemented on branch canvas-ycu-azure-iac, PR #72. Bicep IaC (ACR, private VNet Postgres, Key Vault+managed identity, Container Apps env, API app, migration+seed jobs, Storage static website), root Dockerfile, deploy/pause/resume/destroy.sh mirroring ADP closely. Validated via az deployment sub what-if against the live subscription (20 resources, zero errors) -- NOT actually deployed (az deployment sub create), that real-cost step is left for explicit user decision. Awaiting CI/auto-merge.
close_reason: Merged in #72: Bicep IaC (ACR admin-disabled, private VNet-integrated Postgres with pgcrypto allow-listed, RBAC Key Vault + managed identity, Container Apps env, scale-to-zero API app, migration+seed jobs, Storage static website) + deploy/pause/resume/destroy.sh mirroring ADP closely. Every module validated via az deployment sub what-if against the live subscription (20 resources, zero errors) -- not actually deployed (real cost/access decision left to the user). A real Semgrep finding (Dockerfile running as root) was found and fixed post-merge-request via a follow-up commit before merge. Follow-up filed as canvas-ycu.1 for adding Keycloak itself to this Bicep foundation once canvas-mi9's code integration is ready for it.

title: Integrate Keycloak as the OIDC identity provider, with MFA enforced (Azure deployment)
description:
apps/api/src/auth/oidc.ts already implements generic OIDC SSO (registerOidcRoutes, via the
openid-client package) driven entirely by env vars (OIDC_ISSUER_URL/CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/
REDIRECT_URI, see RUNBOOK.md and apps/api/.env.example) -- in principle any standards-compliant
IdP, including Keycloak, should already work against it. But this has never actually been
exercised against a real IdP: there is no docker-compose service for Keycloak, no realm/client
provisioning, and (critically) apps/web/src/app/LoginForm.tsx has NO link to /auth/login at all --
the frontend only offers local email/password. SSO is currently unreachable from the UI even
though the backend routes exist.

This bead is to actually stand up Keycloak (available as an official Docker image) as the
integration target, wire the frontend to it, and make MFA a real, enforced part of that login
path -- not just something Keycloak is theoretically capable of.

Known gaps found while filing this (not yet investigated further):
1. No docker-compose `keycloak` service, no exported/importable dev realm (client id/secret,
   redirect URIs, roles) for reproducible local iteration -- today OIDC_ISSUER_URL is documented
   to be "left blank locally".
2. apps/web has no "Sign in with SSO" entry point anywhere.
3. oidc.ts's findOrCreateUserFromClaims() hardcodes every newly-provisioned user's role to
   'architect' -- there is no mapping from Keycloak realm/client roles or groups to this app's
   admin/architect role field, so an admin account can't currently be provisioned via SSO at all
   (would need a manual promote via PATCH /admin/users after first login).
4. ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH (apps/api/config.ts) is a full bypass of OIDC/MFA entirely when set -- once
   Keycloak+MFA is the intended primary path in production this needs to be forced off (or made a
   tightly-scoped break-glass path), or MFA is trivially skippable.
5. This app already runs cross-origin on Azure (canvas-eos: COOKIE_SECURE/COOKIE_SAME_SITE,
   docs/azure-deployment.md) -- Keycloak itself will need to be reachable both from the
   Azure-hosted API (server-to-server discovery/token exchange) and from the end user's browser
   (authorization redirect + callback), which commonly means the browser-facing and
   backend-facing Keycloak hostnames differ -- a known class of issuer-URL-mismatch bug with
   Keycloak behind a reverse proxy/ingress. Needs a concrete plan for this deployment's actual
   topology, not assumed to be a single shared hostname.
design:
A sibling project, /home/jmuir/projects/ADP (Python/FastAPI + React, unrelated stack but same
Azure target), already has a complete, production-deployed Keycloak+MFA integration. Read in
full before starting -- specs/026-keycloak-authn/spec.md is the spec to model this bead's own
spec on, and RUNBOOK.md's "Enabling MFA (TOTP)..." / "Frontend auth must stay ON..." sections
document real gotchas hit in their actual Azure deployment, not just design intent.

Concrete, proven answers to this bead's original open questions:

1. AZURE TOPOLOGY (was open, now answered): infra/azure/modules/keycloak.bicep deploys Keycloak
   as a Container App with INTERNAL-ONLY ingress -- never reachable from a browser directly.
   src/adp/api/routers/auth_proxy.py makes the already-public API container transparently
   reverse-proxy everything under /auth/* to it. Keycloak is told its own public base URL via
   KC_HOSTNAME + --http-relative-path=/auth, so it emits correct issuer/redirect URLs itself; the
   proxy does zero path rewriting. Net effect: ONE public hostname, no browser-vs-backend issuer
   mismatch. This pattern should transfer directly to canvas's own Azure deployment (see
   docs/azure-deployment.md) whether or not canvas needs the reverse-proxy piece depends on the
   architecture decision below.

2. MFA ENFORCEMENT (was open, now answered): realm-level otpPolicy* + requiredActions:
   [CONFIGURE_TOTP] in infra/keycloak/adp-realm.json only takes effect on a FRESH realm import
   (Keycloak's --import-realm uses IGNORE_EXISTING). Two real gotchas documented in RUNBOOK.md:
   (a) an already-provisioned realm needs the same settings PATCHed live via the admin REST API
   (src/adp/ops/keycloak_admin_patch.py, KC_PATCH_TARGET=realm) -- (b) requiredActions[].
   defaultAction only auto-assigns via Keycloak's own self-registration/first-login flow, NOT to
   users created through the admin REST API -- src/adp/ops/keycloak_create_users.py sets
   requiredActions: ["CONFIGURE_TOTP"] explicitly per-user for exactly this reason. Any user-
   provisioning approach for canvas that doesn't go through Keycloak's own registration UI needs
   the same explicit-per-user handling or MFA enrollment silently never triggers.

3. ROLE MAPPING (was open, pattern now available): Keycloak groups (EnterpriseArchitect/
   SolutionArchitect/TechnicalArchitect/ADPAdministrator) surfaced in the JWT via a Group
   Membership protocol mapper, then mapped to app roles in src/adp/auth/tokens.py's
   _map_groups_to_role() with an explicit highest-privilege-wins precedence list, defaulting
   unrecognised/no-group users to the lowest-privilege role rather than failing closed or open by
   accident. canvas's oidc.ts findOrCreateUserFromClaims() currently hardcodes every new user's
   role to 'architect' -- would need an equivalent claim-to-role mapping (canvas only has two
   roles, admin/architect, so this is simpler than ADP's four-way split).

4. JWKS FETCH GOTCHA (new, not previously known to be an issue): src/adp/auth/tokens.py's
   _jwks_uri_for() fetches signing keys via the INTERNAL Keycloak URL, not by hairpinning back
   through the API's own public FQDN + the /auth proxy -- that self-loop doesn't route inside
   Container Apps and silently 401s every otherwise-valid token post-login (a black-screen bug
   with no frontend error boundary, per RUNBOOK.md). Only applies if canvas adopts a similar
   internal-ingress+proxy topology for Keycloak.

5. BUILD-TIME ENV BAKING GOTCHA (new): ADP's frontend is Vite-built, same as canvas's apps/web.
   VITE_AUTH_ENABLED/VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL are baked into the static bundle AT BUILD TIME -- a stray
   local .env.local leaking into a production image build silently ships with auth disabled.
   RUNBOOK.md documents a concrete post-build grep check for this. Directly relevant if canvas's
   own Vite build/deploy pipeline doesn't already guard against env-file leakage into CI images.

ARCHITECTURE DECISION THIS BEAD MUST MAKE EXPLICITLY (not yet decided -- ADP's approach does NOT
just drop in):
ADP uses a public SPA OIDC client (keycloak-js in the browser) + Bearer-token-per-request, with
NO backend session -- FastAPI middleware validates the JWT via JWKS on every call
(src/adp/auth/middleware.py). canvas's EXISTING oidc.ts is a fundamentally different, already-
working pattern: a confidential-client, server-side authorization-code+PKCE exchange that
establishes a session COOKIE (@fastify/session), with requireAuth/requireRole
(auth/middleware.ts, auth/access-control.middleware.ts) keyed off req.session.user -- the same
session infrastructure local email/password auth already uses. Porting ADP's SPA+Bearer model
wholesale would mean ripping out canvas's session-cookie auth entirely, a much bigger and riskier
change than swapping in Keycloak as the IdP behind the EXISTING flow (point OIDC_ISSUER_URL at a
Keycloak realm; oidc.ts's authorization-code+PKCE dance already works with any compliant IdP).
Recommendation: keep canvas's session-cookie architecture and use Keycloak purely as the IdP
behind it, rather than adopting ADP's SPA+Bearer model -- reuses already-tested infrastructure
instead of a ground-up auth rewrite. This is a real trade-off worth a conscious decision before
implementation starts, not something to default into silently.

- apps/web has a real "Sign in with SSO" entry point that reaches the existing /auth/login flow.
- Logging in via Keycloak cannot complete without MFA (OTP or equivalent) having been satisfied --
  enforced by realm policy at minimum; open question (see notes) whether the app should also
  defensively check an acr/amr claim rather than trust the IdP's enforcement alone.
- Keycloak-issued users get a real role mapping (at minimum: distinguishing admin from architect

title: Fix style-affordance.spec.ts Clear-button race (canvas-i2q's now-100%-reproducing occurrence)
description: canvas-i2q tracked this as an intermittent flake since PR #41; as of this session (PR #48 x2, PR #49 x1 — three consecutive CI runs) it now reproduces 100% of the time, actively blocking unrelated PRs from merging. Root-caused: style-affordance.spec.ts:110-111 reads dsl-panel's .inputValue() with a single synchronous call immediately after clicking the Clear button, with no retry/polling — if the click's resulting React state update (onChange -> updateNodeStyle(model, id, {fillColor: null}) -> re-render -> DSL panel content) hasn't flushed to the DOM by the time Playwright reads the value, the assertion sees stale content still containing the picked color. Verified updateNodeStyle/mergeStyle (diagram-ops.ts:133-142) themselves are logically correct — null correctly deletes the field — so this is a test-timing bug, not a product bug. Fix: use expect.poll() instead of a single-shot inputValue() read for this specific negative assertion, giving the DOM time to catch up within a bounded timeout, same fix class already suspected in canvas-i2q's own notes (React setState timing vs Playwright's click-then-immediately-read pattern).
acceptance_criteria: style-affordance.spec.ts's 'clicking Clear removes the color override from the DSL' test passes reliably across at least 5 repeated local runs and the next CI run. No product code changed.

title: Diagram creation fails from the ordinary entry point: projectId is URL-only state the UI never sets
description:
Creating a diagram from the ordinary entry point fails with:

  "Missing ?projectId= in the URL — create a project first (User Story 4)."

ROOT CAUSE
projectId is URL-only state that the application reads but never writes. Across all of
apps/web/src only two places touch it: the reader getProjectIdFromUrl() (App.tsx) and
AdminShell's back-link. Every <a href="?..."> in the app is an absolute query-string
replacement, so any click discards it. The only way to hold a projectId is to type it into the
address bar. App.tsx already carries a comment admitting the query param stands in for a project
chooser that was never built.

TWO JOURNEYS REACH IT
1. The ordinary entry point. Land on http://localhost:5173/ with no query string, sign in, click
   New Diagram, pick a type, click Create. This is not an edge case — it is what happens to
   anyone who does not know the parameter exists. Import Diagram and Create with AI fail the same
   way but at least fail on the first click.
2. In-app navigation drops it. home -> admin -> back loses the parameter on the FIRST hop.
   AdminShell's back-link is correct in isolation (it preserves what it is given); the loss is one
   hop earlier, in the ?admin= links that carry no projectId at all — five in AdminShell.tsx and
   five in App.tsx's home nav.

SECONDARY DEFECT
createDiagram() calls setPickingType(false) BEFORE the projectId guard, so the type-picker closes
and the user's chosen diagram type is discarded before the error is shown. Fixable in two lines
independently of the main fix.

WHY THE TEST SUITE NEVER CAUGHT IT — the part worth not re-learning
Every spec that clicks new-diagram, import-diagram-button or create-via-ai-chat first navigates
to /?projectId=${PROJECT_ID}. The only bare page.goto('/') calls are in accessibility.spec.ts
(login-page axe audit, never signs in) and ui-foundation.spec.ts (reads body/button styles, then
re-enters via a helper that supplies the parameter). No test ever reached the home screen without
it, so the defect was structurally invisible to a suite of 83 passing E2E tests. Test fixtures
that always supply a parameter the real UI never sets will hide this whole class of bug — prefer
at least one spec per entry point that navigates the way a user actually would.

OPTION EXPLICITLY REJECTED — do not revisit
"Fall back to the only/first project when the parameter is absent." It looks like the smallest
fix but is wrong: the projects table has no owner or membership column (0001_init.sql), so "the
user's project" is not expressible. The fallback would have to mean "the sole project" or "the
first project", which silently breaks the moment a second project exists, and there is no
GET /projects endpoint today anyway (only POST /projects, GET /projects/:id,
GET /projects/:id/tree).

Also rejected as a complete fix: threading projectId through the ten ?admin= links. It repairs
journey 2 only, leaves journey 1 broken, and makes the bug harder to hit — which is worse than
leaving it obvious.

EVIDENCE
apps/web/tests/e2e/project-context.spec.ts — three tests reproducing the real user journey rather
than hard-coding the parameter. Verified failing 0/3 for the right reasons before any fix:
app-error present where none expected (x2), and searchParams.get('projectId') null after an
admin round trip.
acceptance_criteria: A user landing on the app root with no query string can sign in and create, import, or AI-generate a diagram without touching the address bar. Project context survives navigation to an admin screen and back. The user's diagram-type choice is not discarded when creation cannot proceed. apps/web/tests/e2e/project-context.spec.ts passes without being weakened.

RESOLVED by feature 007 (branch 007-project-context).

Root cause as diagnosed: projectId was URL-only state the UI read but never wrote. Fixed by holding the selected project in application state, seeded from the address and written back with history.replaceState, plus a chooser in the shared header.

Planning uncovered a second, larger problem the bug report did not mention: NO route taking a project id checked anything beyond requireAuth, and getProjectTree read every project and every diagram in the installation with no predicate. Any signed-in user could read any project's whole diagram tree by id. Filtering only the chooser would have hidden project names from a dropdown while leaving them one request away, so server-side enforcement was added: requireProjectAccess on all five routes, projects.owner_id (migration 0006, backfilled), and GET /projects.

Verification: 154 diagram-core, 112 api (was 95), 96 E2E passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed (was 82 passed + 3 failed). The three reproduction tests in project-context.spec.ts pass with the file UNCHANGED (git diff empty) — SC-005.

title: Sign out doesn't terminate the Keycloak SSO session -- immediately re-authenticates on next sign-in
description: POST /auth/logout (apps/api/src/auth/session.ts:32) only destroys canvas-api's own local session cookie ('await request.session.destroy()') -- it never performs an RP-initiated (OIDC) logout against Keycloak. Confirmed by reading apps/api/src/auth/oidc.ts end to end: there is no 'logout'/'end_session' handling anywhere in that file at all, and /auth/login (oidc.ts:180) only ever builds an authorization-code request, never a logout redirect. Keycloak's own browser-side SSO session cookie (set on the /idp origin during the original login) is therefore never cleared by sign-out. Reported symptom, matches this gap exactly: after clicking Sign Out, the user is sent to the SSO sign-in page but is immediately redirected right back into the app, fully signed in again as the SAME user -- Keycloak silently re-issues a fresh auth code because its own session is still alive, so /auth/callback re-establishes a canvas session before the user ever sees a real login prompt. This makes it impossible to sign out and sign in as a different account (e.g. switching between the seeded architect and admin accounts) without a separate mechanism (a private/incognito window, or manually clearing the Keycloak-origin cookie).
acceptance_criteria: Clicking Sign Out terminates BOTH the canvas-api session AND the Keycloak SSO session, so the very next SSO login attempt shows a real Keycloak credential prompt (or account picker) instead of silently re-authenticating the same user. Standard fix shape: /auth/logout redirects (or the frontend redirects after the local logout call succeeds) to Keycloak's end_session_endpoint (`{OIDC_ISSUER_URL}/protocol/openid-connect/logout`) with post_logout_redirect_uri (and id_token_hint if an id_token is retained -- check whether one is currently stored anywhere in the session, since oidc.ts's callback handler may only keep the access token today) pointed back at the app, so Keycloak actually clears its own session cookie before returning control to canvas. Verify end-to-end against the real deployed Keycloak (not just a mock), matching this project's own established 'confirmed live, not just unit tests' precedent for auth-flow changes.
notes: Found live on the Azure deployment (canvas-rg) while testing account switching between the seeded architect (muir.jc@gmail.com) and a newly created admin (admin@example.com) account. Root-caused by code inspection: apps/api/src/auth/session.ts (registerSessionInfoRoutes, /auth/logout) and apps/api/src/auth/oidc.ts (registerOidcRoutes -- no logout/end_session code path exists). title: Sequence: visual authoring for ranged control-flow blocks, notes, activate/deactivate, autonumber
description: Sequence loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect (ranged control-flow blocks, spanning MESSAGES not nodes) and note-left/note-right/note-over (point-in-time notes attached to specific participant(s) via attachedNodeIds) remain DSL-text-only -- no canvas affordance to create any of them. The ranged-block case genuinely needs a NEW selection mechanism this codebase doesn't have yet: selectedEdgeId is deliberately single-select today (see Canvas.tsx's own canvas-u7e comment), so enclosing a RANGE of messages into a loop/alt needs either a new multi-edge-select gesture or an equivalent (e.g. click first+last message in a block). Notes need a new addContainer(attachedNodeIds, sequenceOrder) call wired to a participant-click ('note-left'/'note-right' target one participant, 'note-over' can span more than one) -- addContainer already accepts both fields (canvas-2s6.1), this is UI-only wiring plus computing 'append at end of timeline' the same way addPointMarkerContainer's own maxOrder+1 already does. Separately: activate/deactivate already has full DSL/model/AI-tool support (activateParticipant/deactivateParticipant, diagram-tools.ts:438-458; addPointMarkerContainer, diagram-ops.ts:296-327) but Canvas.tsx never calls it -- pure UI wiring, no new DSL work, cheapest item here. autonumber (DiagramModel.sequenceAutonumber, diagram-model.ts:249-255) has no UI -- add a toggle/checkbox in the diagram toolbar.

close_reason: Sequence visual authoring: (1) Activate/Deactivate -- two toolbar buttons (Activate/Deactivate), enabled with exactly one participant selected, calling the pre-existing addPointMarkerContainer op (pure UI wiring, no new DSL work). Found and fixed a real bug along the way: that op's own 'append after everything on the timeline' maxOrder calc only ever considered CONTAINERS, never edges/messages -- unreachable via its own unit tests (empty-model fixtures) but a real, silent ordering bug the moment a populated timeline existed, which this bead's UI wiring made reachable for the first time. (2) Notes (note-left/note-right/note-over) -- reuses the existing node multi-select (selectedIds) plus a new Kind picker + text field + Add Note button; note-left/note-right require exactly one selected participant, note-over allows several, matching real grammar. Enclosing logic clicks first+last message (the bead's own suggested gesture) and encloses every TOP-LEVEL message whose order falls within that span, not just the literally-clicked ones -- naively moving only the clicked edges while leaving an in-between message at the top level would have silently reordered it to after the whole block on the next save (emitScope sorts each nesting level independently by its own sequenceOrder), a real correctness bug caught during design, not shipped and fixed later. else/and/option branch dividers are deliberately out of scope, matching groupIntoContainer's own identical scope cut. Also widened AddContainerInput with a new style field (rect's color has no separate 'create then patch' op to land on, unlike node/edge style). New unit tests (diagram-ops.test.ts: addPointMarkerContainer's edge-aware maxOrder fix, addContainer's style field, setSequenceAutonumber's full describe block) and a new e2e spec (sequence-block-note-activation-authoring.spec.ts, 12 tests) covering all four sub-features end to end against the real interactive canvas. title: [epic] Visual authoring parity: close DSL-to-canvas-UI gaps across all 6 diagram families
description: Companion to the jmuir-dtu grammar-completeness epic. Two full-codebase audits (2026-09-07) confirmed the 6 supported diagram families (flowchart, sequence, uml, erd, c4, architecture) are largely DSL-grammar-complete, but a real, substantial set of DSL/model constructs have NO visual canvas authoring affordance -- they can only be created by hand-editing the DSL text panel (or via AI chat, which doesn't count as visual authoring). Root cause for most of it: DiagramContainer.role/parentContainerId can never be set by any canvas UI or AI tool, which alone blocks sequence loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/rect/box/notes, UML namespace/note, and C4 boundary-kind selection. This epic tracks closing every disclosed gap so no diagram construct exists in the DSL without a matching way to create/edit it visually. See docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md era plan file (Sonnet session, plan: review-our-current-coverage-lovely-shamir.md) for the full audit writeup and phased design.
design: Phased: Phase 1 (container-role + parentContainerId infrastructure) is foundational and blocks most of Phase 2's per-family children. Phase 2 is 5 per-family vertical slices (sequence/uml/erd/c4/architecture), each bundling any small DSL addition with its matching canvas UI + AI-tool wiring so nothing ships DSL-only. A final polish child covers the remaining pure-UI gaps (style-popup parity, subgraph direction control) that don't need any DSL change at all.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 9 children closed. Every disclosed DSL-to-canvas-UI gap from the original two-part audit (docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md-era plan review-our-current-coverage-lovely-shamir.md) is now closed for all 6 supported diagram families: Phase 1 container-role/parentContainerId infrastructure (canvas-2s6.1) unblocked the five per-family vertical slices (sequence canvas-2s6.2, UML canvas-2s6.3, ERD canvas-2s6.4, C4 canvas-2s6.5, architecture canvas-2s6.6), plus cross-family drag-to-nest (canvas-2s6.8) and the final style-popup-parity/subgraph-direction polish pass (canvas-2s6.7). Two real bugs were found and fixed along the way as their own tracked children rather than silently folded in: canvas-2s6.9 (sequence diagrams silently dropping node/edge style on save/reload) and the setContainerParent cycle guard fixed as part of canvas-2s6.8. No diagram construct exists in the DSL for any of the 6 families without a matching way to create/edit it visually now, closing the epic's own stated goal.

The bead's own 'visually nestable via canvas UI' acceptance criterion surfaced a genuinely bigger finding: Canvas.tsx has ZERO references to parentContainerId anywhere -- there is no drag-to-nest-a-container mechanism for ANY diagram family today, not an architecture-specific gap. description: detect.ts:5 HEADER_TO_FAMILY's C4 pattern is /^C4(Context|Container|Component|Dynamic)$/ -- missing Deployment. c4.ts fully supports C4Deployment once parsing starts (jmuir-dtu.3.2), but a raw C4Deployment import never reaches it since family detection fails first, at the import boundary (apps/api/src/diagrams/import.service.ts). title: ER diagram authoring gaps: cardinality picker, attribute keys/comment, shape restriction
description:
Follow-up to canvas-hox, reported live after that fix shipped -- three concrete remaining gaps in ER diagram canvas authoring:

1. Connect mode's 'Direction' picker (Forward/Reversed/Bidirectional/No arrowhead, canvas-7rr) still applied to ERD even after canvas-hox gave a freshly-drawn connector real default cardinality -- there was no way to CHOOSE cardinality per side, only accept the one-to-many default. A plain arrowhead is not valid ER notation at all, so offering arrow-direction options for ERD was wrong regardless.

2. The ER attribute editor's add-new-attribute row only offered type/name -- no way to mark a new attribute as a key (PK/FK/UK) or attach a descriptive comment, even though EntityAttribute already has both fields and an EXISTING row already had a keys input (just not the add-row, and neither had a comment input at all).

3. The 'Add Shape' toolbar offered all 4 universal shapes (rectangle/rounded-rectangle/circle/diamond) for ERD, and the Icons search palette (scoped to the 'generic' library's shape-alias sentinels, canvas-23t.4) was shown too -- but erd.ts's own parser only ever produces plain rectangles for an entity, so both authored a shape/icon choice the DSL itself has no room for.
design: (1) Two new independent select pickers (connect-er-source-cardinality / connect-er-target-cardinality), shown instead of the Direction picker when dslFamily === 'erd', covering all four real Mermaid ER cardinality options per side (exactly one/zero-or-one/one-or-many/zero-or-many) -- source and target sides use different two-character tokens for the same four options (confirmed against erd.ts's parseCardinalityToken and DEFAULT_CARDINALITY), so two option lists, not one shared list. (2) FieldsPopup's ERD add-row gains keys+comment inputs (attr-new-keys/attr-new-comment) matching the existing row's own fields; existing rows gain a comment input (attr-comment-${id}-${i}) they were missing entirely. (3) getAddableShapes('erd') returns only rectangle; DiagramEditor.tsx hides the whole Palette (Icons) section for dslFamily 'erd'.
acceptance_criteria: Connect mode in an ERD diagram shows two cardinality selects (not Direction), each offering all 4 real options, defaulting to the prior one-to-many default when untouched; picking any combination produces the correct asymmetric DSL token on each side. The fields popup's add-row and existing rows both expose type/name/keys/comment for ERD. The Add Shape toolbar shows only Rectangle for ERD, and the Icons section does not render at all. New/updated e2e coverage for all three; full existing affordance/shape-toolbar regression suite green.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #102: (1) connect mode now shows two independent ER cardinality selects (First/Second entity, all 4 real options each) instead of the arrow-direction picker for dslFamily=erd; (2) FieldsPopup's ERD add-row and existing rows now expose keys+comment, not just type/name; (3) getAddableShapes('erd') returns only rectangle, and the Icons palette is hidden entirely for ERD. Existing flowchart-shape-toolbar.spec.ts ERD case updated to reflect the new correct behavior (moved its old assertion to a UML case). New erd-connect-cardinality.spec.ts + 2 new fields-affordance.spec.ts cases. Full regression across 6 affected e2e spec files green (43/43). Manually verified live against the running app.

title: ER connectors drawn on the canvas showed a plain arrow instead of crow's-foot notation, and could produce unparseable DSL
description:
Reported live: connecting two ER entities via the canvas's own connect-mode gesture (not via DSL) rendered the connector as a plain directional arrow, not real crow's-foot cardinality notation -- wrong ER visual language, and inconsistent with a relationship parsed from DSL text (which correctly shows crow's feet). Root cause: addEdge() is a generic, family-agnostic operation with no erSourceCardinality/erTargetCardinality fields at all, so a freshly-drawn ER edge had neither -- Canvas.tsx's hasErCardinality check (which correctly suppresses the generic arrowhead marker) was therefore always false for such an edge until a save+reparse round-trip re-derived cardinality from erd.ts's own DEFAULT_CARDINALITY serialize-time fallback.

A second, more serious bug was found investigating the first: that same serialize-time fallback (serializeErd) emitted 'A ||--o{ B : ' with an empty label when edge.label was unset (which it always is for a canvas-drawn edge) -- a trailing colon with no label is NOT valid Mermaid erDiagram grammar (RELATIONSHIP_PATTERN's own "(.+)$" requires at least one character, matching real Mermaid). Clicking Apply on that exact freshly-generated DSL text hard-failed with 'Could not interpret line as an entity, relationship, or directive' -- a genuine round-trip break on DSL the app itself had just produced, not just a cosmetic rendering quirk.
design: Fixed at the root rather than papering over it in the renderer: (1) AddEdgeInput/addEdge (diagram-ops.ts) gained optional erSourceCardinality/erTargetCardinality fields; Canvas.tsx's connect-mode handler now passes DEFAULT_ER_SOURCE_CARDINALITY/DEFAULT_ER_TARGET_CARDINALITY (newly exported from erd.ts as the one shared source of truth, replacing erd.ts's own previously-private DEFAULT_CARDINALITY constant) whenever dslFamily === 'erd', so the edge is ER-correct (real cardinality data, crow's-foot rendering) from the moment it's created -- no export-renderer special-casing needed, since svg-renderer.ts's existing hasErCardinality check already keys off the same fields. (2) serializeErd's relationship-line emission now falls back to a DEFAULT_RELATIONSHIP_LABEL ('relates to') whenever edge.label is empty/whitespace-only, guaranteeing valid re-parseable Mermaid regardless of how the edge was created, not just the connect-mode gesture specifically.
acceptance_criteria: A connector drawn via the canvas's connect-mode gesture in an ER diagram shows real crow's-foot cardinality glyphs immediately (no arrowhead), before any save/reload. The DSL panel's own auto-generated text for such a connector re-applies successfully with no error. New regression tests: addEdge's ER cardinality passthrough (diagram-ops.test.ts), and serializeErd never emitting an unparseable empty-label relationship line, including reparse (erd-attributes.test.ts). Manually verified live against the real running app (screenshot) in addition to unit tests.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #101: addEdge() gained optional erSourceCardinality/erTargetCardinality fields; Canvas.tsx's connect-mode handler now supplies real ER cardinality defaults (exported from erd.ts as DEFAULT_ER_SOURCE_CARDINALITY/DEFAULT_ER_TARGET_CARDINALITY) when dslFamily === 'erd', so a canvas-drawn ER connector shows correct crow's-foot notation immediately. Also fixed a genuine round-trip bug found along the way: serializeErd could emit an empty-label relationship line that failed to re-parse -- now falls back to a default label. New regression tests, full diagram-core suite green (691/691). Manually verified live (screenshots) against the real running app.

title: C4 Container()/ContainerDb() macros reject the real 4-arg (id, label, technology, description) form
description: Reported live: a real C4Container bank-example diagram (Container_Boundary with Container/ContainerDb elements) hard-errored on every Container(...)/ContainerDb(...) line with 'Could not interpret line as a C4 element, relationship, or boundary'. Root cause: packages/diagram-core/src/dsl/c4.ts's ELEMENT_PATTERN only ever allowed ONE optional trailing quoted arg (matching Person/System's own '?description' form), but Container/Component's real Mermaid grammar takes TWO optional trailing args -- technology then description -- e.g. Container(api, "API Application", "Java, Docker", "Provides banking functionality..."). Fixed by widening ELEMENT_PATTERN to accept any number of trailing quoted args generically (captured-but-discarded past the label), extending this file's own pre-existing 'capture optionally, don't model' precedent to the whole element-macro family instead of hardcoding a fixed arg count.
acceptance_criteria: The reported DSL (and the general 4-arg Container/ContainerDb form) parses with zero errors; existing 2-arg/3-arg element forms still parse unchanged; new regression tests added; full diagram-core suite green.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #98: widened ELEMENT_PATTERN to accept any number of trailing quoted args (Container/Component's real technology+description form), not just Person/System's single optional description. New regression tests including the exact reported DSL end-to-end. Full diagram-core suite green (687/687).

title: Nested containers (parentContainerId) never get containment-aware geometry — boxes don't actually nest
description:
Live-reported against the real bank-boundary C4 example (canvas-79b's own reproduction, once it could finally parse): 'BankBoundary0 is the outermost. BankBoundary sits within that and BankBoundary2 and BankBoundary3 sit within BankBoundary' -- but none of that nesting is visible in the rendered diagram.

Root cause confirmed precisely: the hierarchy DATA is completely correct -- parentContainerId chains parse right (b1.parentContainerId=b0, b2.parentContainerId=b1, b3.parentContainerId=b1, verified directly). The problem is that nothing ever converts that hierarchy into geometry. Every node AND every container, regardless of nesting depth, gets its position from ONE flat, shared, sequential auto-position counter (c4.ts's nextAutoPosition(), and the equivalent in every other family's parser) that has zero awareness of parentContainerId/containerId. Concretely, from the reported diagram: b0 (outermost) lands at (40,40) with the default 300x200 size; b1 (should be INSIDE b0) lands at (240,180) -- already spilling outside b0's box; b2 and b3 (should be inside b1) land at (640,180)/(640,320) -- floating far to the right with zero geometric relationship to b1 or b0 at all. Every container is an independently-placed 300x200 box on a flat grid; whether one visually overlaps another is pure coincidence.

Not C4-specific -- the same root cause (a flat auto-position counter with no containment awareness) applies to any family with nestable containers: UML namespaces-within-namespaces (jmuir-dtu.2), flowchart subgraphs-within-subgraphs. Not helped by the existing 'Auto Layout' button either -- that feature (canvas-esn) is explicitly flowchart-only AND explicitly does not attempt compound/nested layout by its own design ('full dagre compound-graph/setParent support... an explicit fast-follow, not attempted here since the dagre wiki doesn't document that feature in enough depth to commit to without its own spike').
acceptance_criteria: Not fully specified -- sized like a real feature (spec-kit-worthy per this repo's constitution), not a quick fix, same class as canvas-7vs.1 (sequence lifelines). At minimum needs: each container's rendered position/size actually encloses its own direct child nodes AND child containers (recursively, for arbitrary nesting depth); auto-position logic (or a real layout pass) must be containment-aware instead of a single flat shared counter across every node/container regardless of parentContainerId. Likely intersects with canvas-esn's own explicitly-deferred 'full dagre compound-graph support' fast-follow -- whoever picks this up should check whether that's the right vehicle to extend, or a separate containment-layout pass makes more sense (C4/UML nesting isn't gated to flowchart-family, unlike canvas-esn's own autoLayout() scoping).
notes:
Affects at minimum: C4 (Enterprise_Boundary/System_Boundary/Container_Boundary/Boundary/Deployment_Node nesting, jmuir-dtu.3/.3.2), UML (namespace nesting, jmuir-dtu.2), flowchart (nested subgraphs). Not filed as a child of canvas-7vs (that epic's audit was about fields silently not RENDERED at all -- this is a distinct root cause: the geometry itself was never computed, independent of whether the container draws with role-appropriate styling).
Implemented 2026-09-06: new shared, pure computeContainmentLayout() in packages/diagram-core/src/model/containment-layout.ts -- a two-pass (bottom-up sizing, top-down placement) flow layout with row-wrapping, NOT a full dagre compound-graph solve (same judgment call canvas-esn's autoLayout() already made: not attempted since the dagre wiki doesn't document that feature in enough depth to commit to without its own spike). Wired into c4.ts/uml.ts/flowchart-parser.ts as a post-pass, scoped to a genuinely fresh import (no stored front-matter geometry at all) -- a diagram with existing saved positions keeps the old per-element fallback unchanged (disclosed scope boundary, not a regression). Real bug found+fixed along the way: serializeUml's own canvas.containers front-matter only ever wrote {x,y}, never {width,height} (unlike C4/flowchart's matching serializers), silently dropping a namespace's computed size on first save -- now mirrors C4's pattern exactly. Verified against the exact reported bank-boundary DSL: every boundary now genuinely encloses its children, transitively, confirmed via unit tests (containment-layout.test.ts x6, containment-auto-layout.test.ts x9 -- all 3 parsers, real DSL text, round-trip stability), a live PNG export, and a new containment-layout.spec.ts E2E test against the real interactive canvas. diagram-core 677/677 (was 668). No renderer changes needed -- fix lives entirely in what position/size gets computed at parse time.
Follow-up fix 2026-09-06: a genuinely COMPLETE apps/web E2E run (not the targeted subset the original validation pass used) surfaced a real bug -- the virtual root's own layout inset + a mismatched SIBLING_GAP (20 vs the old flat counter's implicit 40) shifted a simple flat 2-node flowchart's positions, breaking edge-arrowhead-visibility.spec.ts's 2 hardcoded-pixel assertions and label-affordance.spec.ts's connector-affordance test (downstream symptom, same root cause). Fixed: root skips its own inset entirely, SIBLING_GAP raised to 40 -- the common no-containers case is now pixel-identical to pre-canvas-m0g behavior. Confirmed via a full E2E run: 252 passed, 3 skipped (SSO, no Keycloak locally), 0 failed, with AI_PROVIDER=mock matching CI (16 unrelated AI-chat failures under the local real-anthropic-key default were ruled out as a separate, pre-existing, already-documented local-credential issue). Bundled with canvas-7vs.11 into the same still-open PR #92.
close_reason: Every container's rendered position/size now strictly encloses its own direct and indirect children via a new shared computeContainmentLayout(), wired into C4/UML/flowchart's auto-position fallback for fresh imports.

title: C4Context: real bank-boundary example diagram fails to parse (title, Boundary macro, Rel technology arg)
description:
Live-reported: a real-world C4Context diagram (Mermaid's own well-known 'internet banking system' bank-boundary example) was completely unable to render. Traced to 3 distinct, independent parse gaps, all confirmed by running the exact reported DSL directly through parseC4:

1. 'title <text>' -- a real, cross-family Mermaid top-level statement (right after the diagram header) was not recognized at all by c4.ts, hard-erroring the whole file on line 2. Not modeled anywhere in DiagramModel prior to this fix, and (checked) not supported by ANY of the 6 family parsers, not just C4.

2. 'Boundary(b3, "BankBoundary3", "boundary")' -- the generic, no-particular-semantic-type boundary macro (distinct from System_Boundary/Container_Boundary/Enterprise_Boundary) was missing from BOUNDARY_START's keyword alternation entirely, despite being real, common Mermaid syntax (used in Mermaid's own official docs example, which is exactly what was reported here).

title: UML relationship kind (umlRelationKind) never changes edge arrowhead/line rendering
description: DiagramEdge.umlRelationKind ('inheritance'|'composition'|'aggregation'|'association'|'link-solid'|'dependency'|'realization'|'link-dashed'|'lollipop-source'|'lollipop-target') is parsed and modeled correctly (jmuir-dtu.2/.2.1) -- the field's own doc comment in diagram-model.ts explicitly justifies its existence because "a class diagram's arrowhead shape (hollow triangle, filled diamond, ...) carries real semantic meaning [generic arrow/lineStyle] fields' existing values don't fit." title: Sequence 'rect' container highlight color (style.fillColor) hardcoded to none, DSL value ignored
description:

'none'} / fill="${container.style?.fillColor ?? 'none'}"), no new geometry needed.

title: [epic] Renderer completeness: diagram-family fields parsed/modeled but never drawn (post canvas-x66 audit)
