title: ER entity attributes and UML class members are parsed but never rendered (canvas + export)
description:
Reported live: pasting a standard erDiagram with attribute blocks (CUSTOMER { string id ... }) renders only the entity name boxes -- no columns at all. Root-caused precisely: the parser is fully correct (verified by feeding the exact reported DSL through parseErd() directly -- every entity's attributes come back with correct type/name/keys). The bug is entirely in rendering. Neither renderer reads DiagramNode.attributes (ERD) or DiagramNode.members (UML, jmuir-dtu.2) at all:
- packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts's renderNode() draws the node shape plus exactly one centered <text> label (the entity/class name) and stops -- confirmed via grep, zero references to 'attributes' or 'members' anywhere in this file.
- apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx (interactive canvas) has the identical gap -- zero references to either field.

So every ER entity and every UML class with a body renders as a bare labeled box, indistinguishable from one with no attributes/members declared at all, in both the canvas and the exported SVG/PNG. This is a real, live, user-facing completeness gap in two of the six diagram-type families -- ER and UML/class -- not a parser bug and not user error.
acceptance_criteria: Both renderers (svg-renderer.ts for export, shapes.tsx/Canvas.tsx for the interactive canvas) draw a Mermaid-style entity/class 'table': header row = entity/class name (bold or otherwise visually distinct), divider line, then one row per attribute/member below it -- ER: 'type name' plus PK/FK/UK key markers; UML: visibility marker + name (+ type for attributes, or (params): returnType for methods) + static($)/abstract(*) modifier markers, matching how the DSL itself represents these (EntityAttribute / ClassMember in diagram-model.ts). Node box height (and width, if needed to avoid truncation) grows to fit the row count/content -- mirrors the existing content-fit sizing precedent already established for icon nodes (nodeSize/iconNodeSize in svg-renderer.ts, canvas-23t.5). Both renderers must agree pixel-for-pixel per this codebase's existing SC-004 convention (canvas-1rq/canvas-23t.5/flowchart multi-line labels all establish and rely on this same canvas-vs-export parity requirement) -- shared geometry/row-layout helpers exported from svg-renderer.ts and reused by shapes.tsx, not two independent implementations. A node with no attributes/members (e.g. every non-ER/UML diagram, or a bare entity/class declaration) renders exactly as it does today -- zero regression to the other four diagram-type families or to entities/classes with an empty/absent body.
notes: Scope explicitly covers BOTH ER (EntityAttribute) and UML (ClassMember) -- same root cause, same fix shape, confirmed to have the identical gap while investigating the reported ER bug; user opted to fix both together rather than file a second near-identical bug later. Standards enforcement (packages/diagram-core/src/standards/) was not checked for whether it already validates against attributes/members content -- worth a quick look during implementation in case any existing rule silently assumed rendering already worked.
close_reason: Fixed: both renderers now draw a Mermaid-style table body (header + divider + one row per attribute/member) for ER entities and UML classes. tableNodeLayout()/tableNodeSize() added to svg-renderer.ts (shared by shapes.tsx/Canvas.tsx for canvas/export parity, SC-004). No regression to nodes without attributes/members. 10 new contract tests + 3 new e2e tests, all passing (543/543 diagram-core suite, 3/3 e2e).

title: apiapp.bicep AcrPull role assignment fails as 'already exists' on every redeploy, blocking canvas-api updates
description:
Hit live while deploying canvas-5aq's fix: infra/azure/deploy.sh's 'az deployment sub create' (main.bicep -> apiAppDeploy nested deployment) reliably fails with:

  RoleAssignmentExists: The role assignment already exists. The ID of the existing role assignment is 15df6705d73f5a2888f3dd09d1b90dfa.

for modules/apiapp.bicep's acrPullAssignment resource (name: guid(acrId, identityId, 'AcrPull'), scope: resourceGroup()). Reproduced 4 times in a row, including immediately after manually DELETING the conflicting role assignment and letting the redeploy recreate it fresh -- the very next attempt failed the identical way, and a subsequent az role assignment list showed the resource had in fact just been (re)created by that same failed deployment run (createdOn/updatedOn matched the failed run's own timestamp). So this isn't stale leftover state or eventual-consistency lag from an earlier run -- something within the SAME nested apiAppDeploy operation is attempting the identical PUT twice (classic ARM long-running-nested-deployment retry-races-its-own-prior-success pattern for Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, a well-documented class of Azure/Bicep issue since role assignments are immutable/create-only and RBAC replication isn't instantaneous).

Consequence: because apiApp (the actual Microsoft.App/containerApps resource) evidently depends on acrPullAssignment succeeding first, the whole apiAppDeploy nested deployment aborts before ever attempting the container app resource -- confirmed via 'az deployment operation group list --name apiAppDeploy', which showed only 2 operations (the failed roleAssignment, and a Succeeded canvas-identity reference read) -- apiApp itself was never even attempted. So ANY redeploy of apiapp.bicep as currently written is completely blocked until this is fixed; the fix for canvas-5aq had to be shipped by hand via direct 'az containerapp update --image ...' calls, bypassing Bicep entirely for that container app.

keycloak.bicep has the identical acrPullAssignment pattern (separate guid(), 'keycloak' salt) and is presumably equally exposed, just not yet hit because canvas-keycloak wasn't redeployed this session.
design: Root cause not fully diagnosed -- only worked around, not fixed. The 'ARM retries the same nested-deployment PUT internally and the retry collides with the first attempt's own just-created resource' explanation is the leading hypothesis (matches every observed symptom: fails even freshly recreated, fails even after settling time, only 2 operations ever recorded for apiAppDeploy) but has not been confirmed against Azure's own deployment operation correlation IDs/timestamps at sub-operation granularity.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh 'bash infra/azure/deploy.sh' run (or 'az deployment sub create' with an updated apiImageTag/keycloakImageTag) succeeds end-to-end without manual role-assignment deletion or a direct az containerapp update workaround -- i.e. apiAppDeploy's canvas-api container app resource actually gets updated to the new image via the Bicep deployment path. Verify by bumping the image tag and confirming the resulting containerApps revision references it.
notes:
Plausible fixes to evaluate: (1) split acrPullAssignment out of apiapp.bicep/keycloak.bicep into its own separate, idempotent top-level (not nested) deployment/module deployed once, decoupled from the container-app resource's own (slower) provisioning, so it isn't re-PUT on every image-tag-only redeploy; (2) give the role assignment resource an explicit 'existing' guard (a conditional lookup) rather than unconditionally declaring create-semantics every run; (3) remove any implicit dependency forcing apiApp to wait on acrPullAssignment succeeding in the SAME deployment, since the role only needs to exist before the container actually pulls the image, not before the ARM resource write; (4) file/search for the specific upstream Azure/Bicep issue this matches (nested-deployment role-assignment retry-conflicts-with-own-prior-success) for a documented recommended workaround. Whatever the fix, re-verify keycloak.bicep's identical acrPullAssignment isn't equally exposed (untested this session -- canvas-keycloak wasn't redeployed, so it may or may not hit the same failure).

IMPLEMENTED (option 2+3 combined, canvas-0x7's own dedup already having landed since this bead was filed -- apiapp.bicep no longer declares any acrPullAssignment at all, so the exposure moved entirely to keycloak.bicep's single remaining declaration, confirmed still unconditionally re-PUT on every deploy.sh run since main.bicep redeploys every module every time regardless of which image tag changed): modules/keycloak.bicep's acrPullAssignment is now conditional on a new grantAcrPull bool param (default true, so a from-scratch deploy still grants it); main.bicep threads grantAcrPull through to it; deploy.sh resolves the shared identity's principalId (az identity show canvas-identity) and, if it and the ACR both already exist, checks az role assignment list for an existing AcrPull grant on that scope -- passing grantAcrPull=false when found, so a routine redeploy never re-declares (and ARM never re-PUTs) an already-existing assignment at all, sidestepping the retry-race regardless of its exact ARM-internal root cause. Verified: az bicep build on both main.bicep and modules/keycloak.bicep compiles clean (no new warnings), bash -n on deploy.sh passes. NOT YET verified live against a real Azure subscription (this session had no cloud access) -- acceptance criteria's 'bump the image tag and confirm the resulting containerApps revision' step still needs a real redeploy to close this out.

LIVE VERIFICATION COMPLETE (PR #94, canvas-rg in the real Azure subscription, eastus2): ran deploy.sh three times against a genuine from-scratch resource group. Pass 1 (fresh RG) succeeded on foundational resources, failed as documented on Keycloak/migration/seed jobs (secrets not yet seeded -- expected two-pass behavior, unrelated to this bead). Pass 2 was accidentally run against the working tree BEFORE this fix was checked out (a branch-switch mishap) -- it re-declared the same acrPullAssignment with no skip logic at all and succeeded anyway (confirmed via updatedOn changing), suggesting canvas-0x7's earlier duplicate-declaration fix may already cover most of the practical risk on its own at this timing. Also found and fixed a real bug in this fix's own detection query: it checked for the existing AcrPull grant at the ACR resource's own scope, but keycloak.bicep's acrPullAssignment actually declares scope: resourceGroup() -- one level up -- so the check always came back empty and silently fell back to grantAcrPull=true every time. Fixed to check --resource-group directly. Pass 3, on the corrected fix branch, correctly detected the existing grant, printed the skip message, left the assignment's updatedOn timestamp untouched, and completed successfully end-to-end -- canvas-api confirmed running the freshly-built image tag via the normal Bicep deployment path, no manual role-assignment deletion needed. Acceptance criteria met.
close_reason: Live-verified via PR #94 against a real Azure subscription: three deploy.sh runs against a from-scratch canvas-rg, ending with a clean redeploy that correctly skips re-declaring the AcrPull role assignment and completes end-to-end with canvas-api running the new image tag. See notes for full detail including a self-found scope bug in the fix's own detection query, fixed in the same PR.

title: deploy.sh's Keycloak client reconciliation uses direct-grant login, incompatible with Keycloak 25+/26's temporary bootstrap admin
description: Follow-up to canvas-0x7. infra/azure/deploy.sh's 'Reconciling Keycloak's canvas-api client' step authenticates as the Keycloak master-realm admin via grant_type=password direct-grant against admin-cli, to PATCH the canvas-api client's redirectUris/webOrigins/secret to the real production values (the realm export ships a localhost:3000 dev placeholder). This always fails silently (6 retries, then 'WARNING: could not reach Keycloak's admin token endpoint... skipping client reconciliation') because Keycloak 25+/26's KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD-created admin is explicitly a TEMPORARY admin, and Keycloak rejects direct-grant (grant_type=password) for it outright with invalid_user_credentials -- confirmed live, not guessed (a plain curl direct-grant with the correct password fails; the same credentials succeed fine via the browser-style Authorization Code flow with PKCE). Result: every fresh deploy leaves the realm's redirectUris/webOrigins at the dev placeholder, so real SSO login fails with 'Invalid parameter: redirect_uri' until someone manually patches the client (as was done live this session).
design: Rewrite the reconciliation step in deploy.sh to perform the same PKCE Authorization Code flow already proven to work manually this session: (1) GET the master realm's auth endpoint for the security-admin-console client with a generated code_verifier/code_challenge (S256), extract the login form's action URL (session_code+execution) from the returned HTML; (2) POST username=admin&password=$KC_ADMIN_PASSWORD to that action URL, capture the redirect Location header's code= param; (3) exchange that code for an access token via the token endpoint (grant_type=authorization_code, code_verifier); (4) use that token for the existing GET/PUT client-patch logic, unchanged. All of this is scriptable with curl + python3, no new dependencies. Note the temporary admin's token appeared to have only a 60-second expiry in practice -- the whole flow needs to run fast, in as few round trips as possible, and pass secrets via env vars into any inline python (not raw shell string interpolation into source) to avoid an unrelated class of bug also hit live this session.
acceptance_criteria: A genuine from-scratch deploy.sh run (fresh canvas-rg, or at minimum a fresh Keycloak realm/database) successfully reconciles the client automatically -- no manual PKCE workaround needed, no 'skipping client reconciliation' warning, and a real SSO login succeeds on the first attempt after deploy.sh completes.
close_reason:
Fixed via PR #99: replaced the failing grant_type=password direct-grant with the same PKCE Authorization Code flow the Keycloak admin console itself uses. Verified end-to-end against a real, throwaway local Keycloak 26.2 container reproducing the exact production config (start command, KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, --http-relative-path=/idp, real Postgres) -- confirmed 'Created temporary admin user' in its logs (the exact bug scenario), then confirmed the extracted, unmodified reconciliation code from deploy.sh successfully authenticates via PKCE and PATCHes the canvas-api client's redirectUris/webOrigins/secret, verified by reading the client back. Also caught and fixed a real wrinkle along the way: security-admin-console's relative redirect URI must include the /idp prefix or Keycloak rejects the auth request outright.

Honest scope note: this satisfies the bead's own 'at minimum a fresh Keycloak realm/database' alternative bar for the reconciliation mechanism itself, but I did not literally invoke 'bash deploy.sh' (it assumes a full Azure environment throughout, not decoupled to run standalone against just a Keycloak container) nor perform an actual browser SSO login against canvas-api -- both would need a real Azure canvas-rg respin, not done this session (cost/time). If a full live-Azure end-to-end pass is wanted before considering this fully closed, happy to run it -- reopen or ping me.

title: Port Canvas's multi-diagram-type capability into ADP (additive to existing C4 workspace)
description: Follow-up to canvas-hly's feasibility study (docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md, Part 2). Driver: ADP has grown from a Solution-Architect-focused tool into a broader Enterprise/Business Architecture tool, and its C4-only diagramming (React Flow + Structurizr DSL, ElementKind stops at component level) is now too limiting for that scope. Unlike a full replace/merge (Part 1, not feasible -- conflicting source-of-truth models), porting the 5 non-C4 diagram families (flowchart, sequence, ERD, UML, cloud-architecture) is genuinely feasible as an ADDITIVE capability: these have no existing ADP typed-model representation to conflict with, so DSL-as-truth (packages/diagram-core) can simply be adopted for them with zero tension against ArchitectureDescription/adp.store, which stays completely untouched. Two facts verified directly (not assumed): packages/diagram-core has exactly 2 runtime deps (yaml, @dagrejs/dagre), both pure JS, no server coupling -- directly consumable from a browser bundle; ADP's web/ already runs the same toolchain generation as canvas's apps/web (React 18, TS 5.x, Vite, Vitest, Playwright).
design: Phased approach: (1) vendor/publish packages/diagram-core into ADP web/, confirm it builds and its existing test suite runs clean there -- pure spike, no product surface yet. (2) New, independent backend table + minimal FastAPI CRUD router in ADP for the new diagram types' DSL content -- additive only, ArchitectureDescription/adp.store untouched. (3) Port canvas's React canvas-editing components (apps/web/src/canvas/) into ADP's web/src/canvas/, alongside (not replacing) C4Canvas.tsx -- ADP's canvas view gains a diagram-type picker; C4 keeps its existing typed-model pipeline exactly as today. (4) Stretch/later, separately scoped: governance/permissions reconciliation between canvas's admin Standards system and ADP's own RBAC (enterprise_architect/solution_architect/technical_architect/reviewer); linking new diagrams to ADP's traceability model; AI chat integration (canvas's AI-chat tool-calling system is wired to its own provider config/tool surface, distinct from ADP's own LangGraph intake/recommendation/validation pipeline -- explicitly out of scope for a first port). Rendering/export for the new types uses canvas's own SVG renderer directly (pure TS) -- adp.renderer's Python/Structurizr pipeline stays C4-only, untouched. Auth needs no new work -- both already use Keycloak OIDC (infra/azure/README.md already documents this alignment).
acceptance_criteria: Two open product decisions need real answers before implementation starts, not assumptions: (a) is deferring governance/standards-enforcement on the new diagram types acceptable for v1 (recommended: yes, defer); (b) are these new diagrams attached to an ADP Design (part of an EA deliverable) or fully standalone artifacts independent of any design -- this changes the new table's shape. Phase 1 (vendor + build/test spike) should be completed and verified before phases 2-3 are scoped in detail.
notes: Execution moves to ADP's own repo/tracker (/home/jmuir/projects/ADP), using its own speckit setup and its own beads database -- per the user's explicit direction to leave Canvas as a standalone diagram tool, untouched by this effort. This canvas-side bead stays open as the cross-repo reference/pointer to docs/adp-integration-feasibility.md's Part 2 analysis (the phased plan, the two verified portability facts, and the two open product decisions) -- the actual spec/plan/tasks/implementation work will be tracked in ADP's own specs/ and beads, not here.

title: AI chat system prompt doesn't include diagram type or DSL syntax reference
description: apps/api/src/ai/diagram-chat.service.ts's system prompt is built as `${persona?.systemPrompt ?? DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT}\n\n${describeModel(model)}` -- describeModel() summarizes the CURRENT diagram's nodes/edges/containers, but nothing in the prompt tells the model which diagram TYPE it's working with (flowchart vs C4 vs ERD vs UML vs sequence -- apps/api's diagramTypeId) or gives it the actual Mermaid-family DSL grammar/syntax rules for that type (packages/diagram-core's dsl/ parsers already encode this knowledge structurally but it's never surfaced to the model in prose). The model currently has to infer diagram-type-appropriate behavior purely from tool names/descriptions (addNode/addEdge/updateNodeStyle/etc in diagram-tools.ts) with no grounding in the real DSL it's ultimately generating/round-tripping through. This was flagged during 004-ai-diagram-chat's real-provider validation (T033/jmuir-4m0) as a plausible source of subtly-wrong generations once diagram types beyond plain flowchart are exercised with a real (non-mock) LLM, but not investigated further at the time.
design: Open implementation question, not yet decided: how the model actually gets DSL-grammar knowledge. Naive option is inlining a syntax-reference string per diagram type/family directly into the system prompt (diagram-chat.service.ts's describeModel()-adjacent prompt assembly) -- simplest, but bloats every request's prompt tokens/cost even when irrelevant grammar rules never come up in a given conversation, and drifts silently from packages/diagram-core's dsl/ parsers as they gain new syntax (this epic's own jmuir-dtu work is actively expanding several of them) unless kept in lockstep by hand. Before implementing, evaluate whether a proper knowledge-base mechanism is a better fit -- e.g. a retrieval/RAG-style lookup, a tool call the model can invoke on demand ("getDslSyntaxReference(diagramType)") instead of always-injected context, or generating the reference text directly from the parser/serializer source (packages/diagram-core/src/dsl/*.ts, registry.ts) so it can never drift from the real grammar. Decide the mechanism as part of this bead's own implementation, not assumed up front.
acceptance_criteria: A decided (not assumed) mechanism for giving the model real diagramming knowledge, scoped per diagram type/family AND per persona (not diagram-type alone -- see Notes: a Technical Architect needs different reference material, e.g. Microsoft Learn docs for cloud-infrastructure diagrams, than a Business/Enterprise/Solution Architect would) -- inline system-prompt text, an on-demand tool call, generated-from-parser-source reference text, or another knowledge-base approach evaluated against the options in Design. Whichever is chosen, the model's tool calls and any raw-DSL suggestions end up grounded in the real grammar rather than inferred from tool descriptions alone, DSL reference content has a clear story for staying in sync with packages/diagram-core's dsl/ parsers as they evolve (not a hand-copied snapshot that silently drifts), and any persona-specific external knowledge sources compose with personas' existing systemPrompt customization point (ai_personas table) rather than bypass it. Verified against at least one non-mock diagram type (e.g. ERD or C4, not just flowchart) with a real LLM provider, following this repo's existing precedent (T033) of live-provider validation for AI chat changes, not just the mock-NLU e2e suite.
close_reason: SC-002's manual live-provider validation passed against a real Anthropic call (both the bead's own specified ERD test and an additional UML check) -- family-specific tools (setEntityAttributes, setRelationshipKind, setClassMembers) fire correctly and produce real, type-correct DSL syntax, not generic labeled boxes.

title: Add Keycloak as an Azure Container App to canvas-ycu's Bicep foundation
description:
canvas-mi9 shipped the Keycloak/MFA CODE integration (SSO login flow, realm-role-to-UserRole
mapping, MFA enforcement) and verified it end-to-end against a real local Keycloak instance (see
RUNBOOK.md's "Keycloak SSO" section) -- but canvas-ycu's Bicep foundation (infra/azure/) does not
yet deploy Keycloak itself as an Azure resource. A deployment of that IaC today has no OIDC
provider reachable at all, so ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH stays true by default there (apiapp.bicep's own
param comment documents this as a deliberate, temporary decision, not an oversight).

infra/azure/README.md's "Not included" section already lists exactly what this follow-up needs,
written at the time canvas-mi9 shipped:
- A new modules/keycloak.bicep: internal-ingress-only container app (never reachable from a
  browser directly), mirroring /home/jmuir/projects/ADP/infra/azure/modules/keycloak.bicep.
- A reverse-proxy route on apiapp.bicep's own container forwarding /auth/* (or similar) to
  Keycloak's internal FQDN, mirroring ADP's src/adp/api/routers/auth_proxy.py -- so the browser
  only ever talks to the one already-public canvas-api hostname, avoiding a browser-facing-vs-
  backend-facing issuer URL mismatch.
- OIDC_ISSUER_URL on apiapp.bicep set to the resulting public https://<api-fqdn>/auth/realms/
  CanvasRealm address; Keycloak's own KC_HOSTNAME told to believe that's its own address.
- A real (non-dev-fixture) user-provisioning story -- infra/keycloak/CanvasRealm-realm.json's two
  seeded users are for local iteration only. Mirroring ADP's keycloak_create_users.py is one
  option, including its own documented gotcha: requiredActions[].defaultAction does NOT
  auto-assign to admin-API-created users, only Keycloak's own self-registration/first-login flow,
  so MFA enrollment must be set explicitly per user or it silently never triggers.
- apiapp.bicep's allowLocalAuth default flipped to false once the above actually lands, or MFA
  stays bypassable via the local-auth path even with Keycloak deployed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Keycloak deploys as an internal-ingress Container App via a new modules/keycloak.bicep, wired
  into main.bicep alongside the existing modules.
- The API app reverse-proxies requests to Keycloak so the browser only ever reaches the one
  public canvas-api hostname; issuer/redirect URLs actually match end to end (verified against a
  real deployed instance, not just what-if).
- A decided (not silently deferred a second time) real-user-provisioning approach for the deployed
  realm.
- apiapp.bicep's allowLocalAuth flipped to false, with MFA genuinely required to sign in to the
  deployed environment.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #74 (merged): modules/keycloak.bicep (internal-ingress Container App), /idp/* reverse proxy on canvas-api, internal/public issuer split, real user provisioning via create-users.mjs + canvas-keycloak-users job, deploy.sh client reconciliation, allowLocalAuth now defaults false. Also fixed a real .dockerignore bug (bare *.tsbuildinfo pattern only excluded build-context-root files) found while validating.

title: Session cookies break on a split-origin deployment (e.g. Azure): no trustProxy, hardcoded SameSite=Lax
description: Deployed the app to Azure (App Service for the API, Storage static website for the frontend -- a genuinely split-origin, cross-site topology) and found two real bugs, previously worked around only by hand-patching the deployed dist/ output (not committed): (1) app.ts's Fastify instance had no trustProxy option -- Azure App Service terminates TLS at its edge and forwards to the Node process over plain HTTP internally, so without trustProxy, a Secure-flagged cookie was silently never issued (no error -- login returned 200 with the correct user body, but no session cookie was ever set). (2) session.ts hardcoded sameSite: 'lax' and tied secure only to NODE_ENV==='production' -- SameSite=Lax cookies are never attached to cross-site fetch/XHR calls (only top-level navigation), so even with the cookie being issued, a split-origin frontend's API calls would never carry it back, surfacing as a persistent 'Authentication required' error right after an apparently-successful login.
acceptance_criteria: app.ts sets trustProxy: true (harmless with no reverse proxy in front -- only takes effect when X-Forwarded-* headers are present). config.ts exposes cookieSecure/cookieSameSite, driven by new COOKIE_SECURE/COOKIE_SAME_SITE env vars, defaulting to the exact previous same-origin-safe behavior (no Secure flag, SameSite=Lax) so local dev and any same-origin deployment need no changes. COOKIE_SAME_SITE=none forces cookieSecure=true regardless of COOKIE_SECURE (SameSite=None without Secure is invalid and browsers reject it outright). Documented in RUNBOOK.md and a new docs/azure-deployment.md capturing the full working deployment process.
notes: Found and root-caused live against a real Azure deployment (App Service + Postgres Flexible Server + Storage static website), not simulated. Verified the fix via a real regression test that logs in, captures the actual Set-Cookie header, and replays it on a follow-up request with X-Forwarded-Proto: https -- confirming the exact failure mode (cookie issued but the session never actually usable) is closed, not just that a cookie exists.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #65 (merged). app.ts: trustProxy: true. config.ts: new cookieSecure/cookieSameSite driven by COOKIE_SECURE/COOKIE_SAME_SITE env vars, defaulting to the exact previous same-origin-safe behavior. session.ts uses them instead of hardcoded sameSite:'lax'. New docs/azure-deployment.md and RUNBOOK.md updates. New session-cookie.test.ts contract test reproduces the exact failure mode via X-Forwarded-Proto and confirms it's closed.

title: Multi-select on the diagram canvas: Ctrl+click toggle and drag/rubber-band marquee select
description: Canvas.tsx's multi-select is currently limited to Shift+click toggling one node at a time into/out of selectedIds (a Set<string>) -- confirmed via code read, no other path adds to it. Two gaps versus standard Windows diagram-app conventions (Visio, PowerPoint, draw.io): (1) no Ctrl+click toggle-select, only Shift+click works, and (2) no drag/rubber-band (marquee) selection at all -- clicking and dragging on empty canvas background does nothing (a plain onClick on the <svg> only clears the current selection; there is no pointer-down-drag-pointer-up rectangle-select flow). Both are baseline-expected behavior for selecting multiple objects on a 2D canvas.
design: Needs its own investigation/plan before implementing -- not started yet. Open questions to resolve: does the marquee rectangle need full-containment or just intersection to select an item; does it include containers and edges or nodes only for v1; how does starting a drag on the empty canvas interact with the existing dragState ref used for moving a single node/container (dragState.current currently only has a 'node'/other kind, would need a new 'marquee' kind); rendering the live selection rectangle (a simple <rect> overlay, removed on pointerup) needs a new bit of transient state.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+click a node toggles it into/out of the current multi-selection, same as Shift+click does today (both work, matching common app conventions where either modifier works interchangeably in a freeform canvas context). Click-dragging on empty canvas background draws a visible selection rectangle; on release, every node (and reasonably, container/edge -- scope TBD by implementer) whose bounds intersect (or are fully contained by, TBD) the rectangle is added to the selection. Existing single-click-select-one and Shift+click-toggle behavior is unchanged. Existing Group-into-Container/Delete-Selected actions (which already key off selectedIds.size) work unmodified with a marquee-built selection.
notes: Implemented on branch canvas-558-multi-select, PR #68 (separate from the canvas-23t epic bundle in PR #67, since it's not a child of that epic). Ctrl/Cmd+click toggle-select and drag/rubber-band marquee select (intersection-based, additive with modifier held, nodes-only for v1). New e2e spec multi-select.spec.ts (6 tests, all passing). Awaiting CI/auto-merge.
close_reason: Merged in #68: Ctrl/Cmd+click now toggles a node into/out of the selection like Shift already did. Dragging on empty canvas background draws a rubber-band marquee (intersection-based hit test, additive with a held modifier, nodes-only for v1 -- containers/edges keep their existing separate single-select state). New multi-select.spec.ts (6 e2e tests). Full repo e2e regression: 215/216 passed (1 pre-existing skip).

title: Node label text overflows its box with no wrapping (most visible on Azure icon labels)
description:
A node's label renders as a single SVG / line with no width-aware wrapping -- splitLabelLines only breaks on explicit
or a raw newline (grouping F, flowchart-completeness-brief). Any label wider than the node's own box (140x60 default) overflows both left and right edges uncontained. Most visible on icon nodes placed from the Azure/AWS libraries, whose displayName is often a long descriptive product name (e.g. 'Azure Storage Accounts', 'Azure Data Virtualization') -- ordinary flowchart shape labels are usually short enough to rarely trigger this, but icon labels routinely do. Reproduced live: placing an 'Azure Storage Accounts' icon renders its label bleeding well past the node's rectangle on both sides.
acceptance_criteria:
A long node label (e.g. an Azure icon's displayName) wraps onto multiple lines within the node's own width instead of overflowing, in both the interactive canvas and the export renderer (SC-004 -- they must agree). Existing explicit
-driven multi-line labels (grouping F) are unaffected. Short labels that already fit on one line render exactly as before (no regression).
close_reason:
Shipped via PR #63 (merged). Extended splitLabelLines with optional maxWidth/fontSize params to word-wrap a label too wide for its node's box, on top of grouping F's existing explicit-
-break splitting. Wired into both renderNode (export) and Canvas.tsx's own label rendering. Fixes the reported overflow, most visible on Azure/AWS icon labels (e.g. 'Azure Storage Accounts').

title: Add dagre-based Auto Layout for flowchart-family diagrams
description: No way to auto-arrange a diagram exists today -- every node/container position is set manually (drag, or the grid-placement fallback used when adding a shape). DiagramModel.direction and DiagramContainer.direction already exist and round-trip through the DSL but neither drives layout. User supplied docs/mermaid_dagre_demo.html and the dagre wiki (https://github.com/dagrejs/dagre/wiki) as the layout engine to use. Adds an 'Auto Layout' toolbar action, scoped to flowchart-family diagrams for v1, using @dagrejs/dagre to compute node/container ranks and positions from the model's edges.
design: See /home/jmuir/.claude/plans/groovy-snuggling-hopcroft.md for the full approved plan. Key decisions: flowchart-family scope only (not C4/architecture/ERD/UML, never sequence); v1 does FLAT layout only (top-level nodes/containers laid out by dagre, contents of a container keep their relative position via existing moveContainer() reuse -- full compound-graph/cluster support deferred, dagre wiki doesn't document it in enough depth); dagre added to packages/diagram-core (new autoLayout() pure operation, second real runtime dep after yaml); edges stay straight-line (no dagre polyline routing in v1).
acceptance_criteria: A user can click 'Auto Layout' in the canvas toolbar (with a TD/LR/BT/RL direction picker) on a flowchart-family diagram and see nodes/containers rearranged into a sane, non-overlapping layout reflecting the DAG structure of the diagram's edges. model.direction updates to match and round-trips through Save/reload via the existing DSL 'graph <direction>' token. Nodes already inside a container keep their position relative to it. Contract tests in packages/diagram-core and an e2e spec in apps/web cover the above.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #61 (merged). New autoLayout() pure operation in packages/diagram-core backed by @dagrejs/dagre; a new Auto Layout button + TD/LR/BT/RL direction picker in Canvas.tsx's toolbar, gated to flowchart-family diagrams. v1 is flat (top-level nodes/containers only, container contents keep their relative position via the existing moveContainer()).

title: Dev DB's seeded E2E_PROJECT_ID no longer exists; 594 unpaginated test-debris projects now breaking specs
description: While independently re-verifying canvas-3vq.1's new e2e spec, running the broader Projects-adjacent spec suite (project-rename-move, projects-page, project-context, project-visibility, project-delete-restore, delete-restore-diagram) against the shared dev DB surfaced 3 failures, all in specs that reference the fixed E2E_PROJECT_ID from .claude/settings.local.json (172794e4-2fb8-4f30-afae-41f4262c1a27). Confirmed via direct DB query: that project no longer exists at all (SELECT ... WHERE id=... returns zero rows) — likely deleted incidentally by one of this session's own delete/restore-project e2e runs, since nothing in the app has a UI-level 'permanently purge' path outside admin restore-window expiry. Separately, live project count is now 594 (SELECT count(*) FROM projects WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), up from the 380 docs/navigation-flow-brief.md measured only a day earlier — confirms that brief's §9 open question 3 concern (accumulated e2e-test debris making the dev DB steadily less usable for manual verification and slower for any spec that renders the full project list) is actively getting worse, not just a one-time observation. Not fixed as part of canvas-3vq.1 (out of scope — that bead's own new spec creates its own per-test projects and is unaffected) but needs its own attention: either reseed and update E2E_PROJECT_ID everywhere it's hardcoded (.claude/settings.local.json, RUNBOOK.md, CI env), or move every remaining spec that still depends on one shared fixed seeded project over to the create-your-own-project-per-test pattern most newer specs (project-rename-move.spec.ts, project-browser-search.spec.ts) already use, eliminating the shared-fixture dependency entirely.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) the dev DB is reseeded and every hardcoded E2E_PROJECT_ID reference is updated to the new id, or (b) no e2e spec depends on a single shared seeded project id anymore — pick one, don't half-do both. Whichever direction: a full e2e suite run in this environment shows zero failures attributable to a missing/stale seeded project.
notes: Confirmed via a full e2e suite run (181 tests) while working on canvas-0s3: the stale seeded E2E_PROJECT_ID (172794e4-...) cascades into 7 of 10 total failures across delete-diagram-permission-error, project-context, project-rename-move, project-visibility, projects-page, and sharing specs — all either navigate directly to ?projectId=<stale-id> or assert its row/URL exists. The other 2 (shared-diagrams.spec.ts, both tests) match canvas-mt3's already-documented guest@example.com share-grant accumulation exactly. None of the 10 failures touch canvas rendering/interaction code — confirms canvas-0s3's changes introduced zero regressions.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #56 (merged). Playwright globalSetup hook (apps/web/tests/e2e/global-setup.ts) now auto-resolves E2E_PROJECT_ID via the existing idempotent 'npm run seed' Smoke Test project lookup-or-create whenever nothing has already set it explicitly -- self-healing if that project is ever deleted again, no more manually-exported stale ids. CI's own explicit E2E_PROJECT_ID setting is untouched (explicit override always wins). Verified: tsc/eslint clean, new global-setup.spec.ts (2 tests, no test.skip guard by design) passing, full local e2e suite 192 passed/1 skipped/1 failed (failure is the separate, already-tracked canvas-mt3, now itself being fixed).

title: Client-side filter over ProjectsPage's already-fetched project list (US3)
description: US3 from docs/navigation-flow-brief.md §7 (Finding B, project-level). No server-side query support exists for GET /projects (project.routes.ts:58-60 takes no params; project.service.ts:69-75's own comment: 'No search or paging: the clarified scale is tens of projects'). A live scale-check against the seeded dev DB found 380 projects visible to one admin user (caveated: largely e2e-test debris, e.g. epoch-millisecond-suffixed names, not evidence of real organic usage — but the unbounded-render shape of the problem is real regardless). Since GET /projects already returns the full list in one call, add a plain client-side filter over the already-fetched array in ProjectsPage.tsx — zero API change, ships immediately, matches VersionHistory's existing search-input styling.
design: Explicitly NOT server-side — that's US4 (separate, gated bead), only worth doing if/when real non-test-debris project counts justify it.
acceptance_criteria: ProjectsPage has a search input that filters the rendered project list client-side by name as-you-type; no new network calls introduced; existing create/rename/delete actions unaffected.
close_reason: Shipped: PR #49 merged. Added a plain client-side filter (projects-page-filter) over ProjectsPage's already-fetched project list -- zero API change, no network request per keystroke. Required a manual merge-conflict resolution against ProjectsPage.tsx (PR #48's View Diagrams action touched the same row-rendering block after PR #49's last CI pass, so GitHub's auto-merge never actually fired despite the checks staying green) -- resolved by keeping the filter's outer wrapping (search input, filteredProjects.map, empty-match state) with the row content from main (View Diagrams button, unconditional row__actions span, Rename/Delete still gated by canManage inside it). e2e-tested (4 tests: narrows+hides distractor, empty-match state, clear restores full list, existing row action still works while filtered).

title: Epic: Projects/Diagrams navigation flow — Option A (connect existing screens)
description: Source: docs/navigation-flow-brief.md, a design review requested directly (not part of docs/ui-review-brief.md's groupings). Today ProjectBrowser (diagram tree, 'current project' scoped), ProjectsPage (flat management list, all projects), and the header ProjectPicker are three screens/widgets that never reference each other — e.g. ProjectsPage's rows have no way to actually go look at that project's diagrams (brief §2, Finding A). Separately, GET /projects/:projectId/diagrams?query=&type= is a fully built, perf-tested (1,200 diagrams) search endpoint the frontend never calls at all (brief §3, Finding B). Two directions were laid out in §6: Option A (incremental — connect what exists, keep ProjectBrowser as default landing screen, cheap, doesn't touch the 14+ e2e specs anchored on today's landing behavior) vs Option B (structural — unify into one drill-in browsing surface, retire 'current project' as global state, real rewrite touching App.tsx's core state model and withProjectContext). Decision made: start with Option A now (this epic); Option A's pieces (View Diagrams action, breadcrumb) deliberately survive a later Option B merge rather than being thrown away. Option B itself is tracked separately as a deferred/gated placeholder (see linked bead) — not started, needs its own future decision to actually kick off.
design: Sequencing per brief §7: US1 and US2 are independent, either can go first; US3 can ship alongside or after either.
acceptance_criteria: All three Option-A child stories (US1 diagram search, US2 ProjectsPage->ProjectBrowser drill-in link, US3 client-side project filter) shipped and merged.
close_reason: Epic complete: all three Option-A children shipped. canvas-3vq.1 (PR #46/#47): wired ProjectBrowser's diagram search/type-filter to the pre-existing, perf-tested GET /projects/:projectId/diagrams endpoint. canvas-3vq.2 (PR #48): ProjectsPage gained a 'View Diagrams' action and ProjectBrowser gained a breadcrumb back-link, closing the one genuine dead end in the IA (brief Finding A). canvas-3vq.3 (PR #49): client-side name filter over ProjectsPage's project list. Option B (canvas-t3b, the structural unification of ProjectsPage/ProjectBrowser) remains deferred as its own epic, per the brief's own recommendation -- not started, no decision yet to pursue it over continuing to iterate on Option A.

title: Color-picker affordance for shapes and connectors (fill/stroke color on canvas)
description: NodeStyle (fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWidth/strokeDasharray) is already a full model field, and canvas-kwa added updateNodeStyle/updateEdgeStyle diagram-core operations + AI tool wrappers so chat can color shapes/connectors on request. There is still no manual way to do this on the canvas itself — only via AI chat or hand-editing the DSL panel's style/classDef/linkStyle syntax directly. Extends the existing pencil edit-affordance area with a second, separate icon/button that opens a small color-picker popup: fill color for shapes, stroke/line color for connectors. Requires no backend/model/rendering/DSL changes beyond a small diagram-core extension to support explicitly clearing a style field (today updateNodeStyle/updateEdgeStyle can only ever set a field, never clear one back to unset) — DSL round-trip and both renderers already fully respect style.fillColor/strokeColor.
design: Plan file: /home/jmuir/.claude/plans/groovy-snuggling-hopcroft.md. Key decisions (confirmed with user): (1) separate new icon/button next to the existing pencil, not merged into the same popup — lowest risk against label-affordance.spec.ts's 5 existing assertions; (2) Clear/Reset is in scope, requiring StylePatch fields to become string|null (null=clear, undefined=leave alone) in diagram-ops.ts's mergeStyle. New foreignObject popup (~120x56) with a native input type=color, Clear button, explicit Done button (not blur-only, given native color-picker focus-timing quirks). Container styling out of scope (no existing pencil affordance for containers either).
acceptance_criteria: A user can open a color picker for any node or edge directly from the canvas (new affordance next to the existing pencil), pick a fill color (nodes) or stroke color (edges), see it applied immediately, clear it back to default, and have it persist through save/reload/export. Existing label-affordance.spec.ts (5 assertions) passes unchanged.
close_reason: Merged in PR #36 (feat) and #37 (docs). Second, separate palette icon next to the existing pencil opens a color-picker popup (fill for shapes, stroke for connectors), reusing updateNodeStyle/updateEdgeStyle. StylePatch widened to support explicit-null-clears semantics, test-first. Visual polish by ui-design-expert subagent; functional e2e coverage (9 new tests) by tester subagent, which found 2 real bugs (Escape not closing popup, edge affordance unclickable in standard layout) — both fixed and re-verified. Full e2e suite 148/149 pass, sole failure is pre-existing unrelated canvas-mt3.

title: AI capabilities aren't visibly gated when chat is admin-disabled or running on the mock provider
description:
Confirmed via code: neither App.tsx nor DiagramEditor.tsx ever reads ai_settings.chatEnabled — the 'Create with AI' button (App.tsx) and the editor's Chat rail tab are always shown enabled regardless of the admin toggle. The only enforcement is server-side (diagram-chat.routes.ts returns 503 when chatEnabled is false) — an architect can click into the flow, type a full message, and only then hit a failure, instead of the feature being visibly unavailable up front.

Separately: AiSettingsDto (api.ts) only exposes { chatEnabled: boolean } — there is no way for the client to know which AI_PROVIDER is actually configured server-side. server.ts's own comment says AI_PROVIDER=mock is 'for E2E/local testing only... a real deployment sets AI_PROVIDER=anthropic|openai and this branch never runs' — but if a real environment is ever misconfigured to mock (this exact drift happened repeatedly THIS session via tsx watch losing env vars on restart), users would silently get the rule-based fake NLU (which only recognizes a handful of canned phrases and otherwise replies 'I'm not sure how to help with that') with no indication AI isn't really active.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The AI entry points (Create with AI button, Chat tab) are visibly disabled/greyed with an explanatory message when ai_settings.chatEnabled is false, checked client-side before the user can even start typing — not just a 503 after the fact. 2) The admin-settings response gains a provider indicator (e.g. is this the mock/placeholder provider or a real one) and the same entry points show a clear 'AI is running in test/mock mode' indicator when applicable, so a misconfigured environment is obvious rather than silently degraded.
notes: Filed from a live user observation. Confirms a real, verified gap on both counts via direct code inspection (grep for chatEnabled/getAiSettings usage in the frontend, and AiSettingsDto's field list).
close_reason: Merged in #69 (after a CI re-run resolved a pre-existing flaky sharing.spec.ts failure unrelated to this change): App.tsx's Create with AI button and ChatPanel.tsx's composer now check ai_settings.chatEnabled client-side before the user can type, via a new GET /ai-settings (any authenticated user, mirrors /ai-personas vs /admin/ai-personas). Both also show a 'running in test/mock mode' note when AI_PROVIDER resolves to mock, via a new resolveAiProviderKind(). PersonaAdminPage gains a read-only provider indicator. 204 API tests + 21 e2e tests passing.

title: Canvas has no way to pan/scroll to content placed beyond its fixed 800x500 viewport
description: Canvas.tsx's <svg> is hardcoded at width={800} height={500} (never computed from actual node/container positions, unlike the export renderer's computeBounds in svg-renderer.ts). The surrounding .editor__canvas container already has overflow: auto (layout.css), but since the SVG child element's own laid-out size never exceeds 800x500 regardless of where shapes are dragged, the browser never has anything to scroll to — there's nothing overflowing the container's box. A shape dragged/placed beyond x=800 or y=500 becomes clipped and effectively unreachable: no scrollbar appears, and there's no pan/zoom gesture either.
acceptance_criteria: A user can reach and interact with shapes placed anywhere on the canvas, not just within the initial 800x500 area — either by the SVG growing to fit actual content (enabling the container's existing overflow:auto to produce real scrollbars) or a dedicated pan/zoom mechanism. Existing shape/edge/container rendering and interaction must be unaffected.
notes: User-observed refinement: left-to-right is fine, top-to-bottom is not. The editor's canvas column is apparently close to 800px wide (matching the SVG's hardcoded width, so no visible horizontal gap), but the .editor__canvas container is much taller than the SVG's hardcoded 500px height on typical viewports — the dot-grid background (painted on the container, not the SVG) fills the full container height, so the bottom portion of the visible screen LOOKS like drawable canvas but is actually outside the SVG's bounds and gets clipped/unreachable. Same root cause as the original report (hardcoded 800x500 SVG size), just far more visually obvious vertically than horizontally given typical viewport aspect ratios.
close_reason: Shipped: PR #51 merged. Canvas.tsx's SVG now sizes itself to Math.max(visible container via ResizeObserver, actual content bounds via newly-exported computeBounds from svg-renderer.ts), so .editor__canvas's overflow:auto finally produces real scrollbars for content beyond the old fixed 800x500. Two real regressions found and fixed during implementation (not just the planned Canvas.tsx/CSS change): (1) .editor__body's CSS grid had no grid-template-rows, so its implicit row auto-sized to content instead of staying capped at available viewport space; (2) .app-shell used min-height:100vh (a floor, not a cap), so a tall canvas grew the whole page instead of scrolling internally -- fixed via height:100vh + overflow-y:auto on .app-content (verified this doesn't regress the Projects list's own scroll). A third, subtler regression (edit-labels.spec.ts's edge dblclick landing in empty space once the container's height became viewport-fit-exact instead of a fixed 500px) was root-caused via careful bisection and fixed as a test-robustness improvement (target the line's own point, not the group's raw bbox center) -- confirmed via cross-branch comparison this was Playwright click-point fragility, not a real end-user-facing bug, since the affordance icons themselves remained clickable throughout.

title: Connectors (edges) cannot be selected or deleted directly on the canvas
description: Canvas.tsx imports removeEdge from @canvas/diagram-core but never calls it anywhere. Edges only get onPointerEnter/onPointerLeave (hover, for the edit-label affordance) and onDoubleClick (opens the label editor) — no onPointerDown handler at all, so edges are never added to selectedIds (that state is only ever populated by handleNodePointerDown for nodes). requestDeleteSelected/confirmDeleteSelected and the Delete/Backspace keyboard shortcut only ever operate on selectedIds (nodes) and selectedContainerId (containers). The only ways to remove a connector today: delete one of its endpoint nodes (removeNode cascades and removes attached edges as a side effect — but also destroys the node, not a targeted fix), or hand-edit the DSL panel directly. A shape's delete workflow (click to select, Delete Selected button or Delete/Backspace key) has no connector equivalent at all.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a connector selects it (some clear visual indicator, consistent with node selection's blue outline). A selected connector can be removed via the same Delete Selected button and Delete/Backspace shortcut nodes already use, calling the existing removeEdge operation. Removing a connector must not affect its endpoint nodes.
notes: Found while working the canvas-7rr connector-direction feature — noticed removeEdge was imported but dead code.
close_reason: Shipped: PR #52 merged. Canvas.tsx imported removeEdge but never called it -- edges had no selection state, no click handler, no way to delete short of removing an endpoint node (destroys the node) or hand-editing the DSL. New selectedEdgeId state (single-select, mirroring selectedContainerId's own pattern) tracks which edge, if any, is selected; a new handleEdgePointerDown sets it and clears any node/container selection (mutually exclusive, matching existing node/container precedent). A selected edge's <line> turns the same SELECTION_STROKE blue used for node selection (now exported from shapes.tsx for reuse). The existing Delete Selected button and Delete/Backspace shortcut now also work when only an edge is selected, calling the existing removeEdge operation via the same confirm-dialog flow with a new connector-specific message. removeEdge only ever touches the edge itself -- endpoint nodes untouched, verified live and in the new e2e spec (6 tests, 12/12 runs passing, no product bugs found by tester subagent or my own independent re-verification).

title: Add project rename (update) and move-diagram-between-projects
description: No updateProject API/route exists — a project's name is permanent once created. There is also no UI to move an existing diagram to a different project. Per the approved plan (canvas-228 epic): rename is a click-to-edit control on the Projects screen (canvas-228.1), gated to the project's owner or an admin (new requireProjectOwnerOrAdmin middleware). Move is a new 'Move' action on each diagram row in ProjectBrowser.tsx, gated to anyone with edit access to the diagram (matching the permissiveness of every other diagram edit) plus edit access on the destination project.

title: Icon palette surfaces broken "generic" shape-alias entries — needs a product decision
description:
US4 from docs/ui-review-brief.md §4, addressing finding #4.

Every diagram type's default_palette_library_ids includes "generic" (confirmed via DB:

Placing one via the icon path produces a shape:'icon' node that resolves to NO artwork at all —

(c) visually mark shape-alias results in search (e.g. a distinct tile style) so a user isn't
fooled before placing one.
Needs a stakeholder decision before /speckit-specify or implementation proceeds — same "flag it,

title: apps/api test suite TRUNCATEs the same DB the interactive dev server uses (no isolated test DB)
description:
apps/api/tests/helpers/setup.ts's resetDatabase() runs TRUNCATE ... CASCADE against whatever DATABASE_URL is loaded from apps/api/.env, with no separate test-database override. That .env is the same one the long-running dev server (npm run dev) and npm run seed use. Running npm run test --workspace=@canvas/api (or any single contract test file) during a dev/E2E session wipes users, projects, diagrams, everything — with no restoring afterward.

Hit this directly: mid-session, ran the full apps/api suite to validate an unrelated change, which silently destroyed the seeded dev project/users the E2E suite depended on. Recovery was non-obvious: npm run seed's ensureUser() short-circuits on an existing email (apps/api/src/seed/run.ts:27-28) without recreating local_credentials, so if a test's own seedUser() (same email, different password, e.g. libraries.test.ts:34 uses 'admin@example.com'/'admin-pass') leaves a row behind, a subsequent npm run seed silently leaves that mismatched password in place instead of restoring 'admin-dev-password' — login then fails with no indication why. Required manually re-running the TRUNCATE + npm run seed together to recover.

Fix needs a real isolated test database (separate DATABASE_URL for NODE_ENV=test, e.g. a distinct db name/port), not the dev DB — this is a standard test-isolation gap, not something specific to any one feature.
acceptance_criteria: Running npm run test --workspace=@canvas/api never mutates the database the dev server (npm run dev) or npm run seed use. A test run followed immediately by continued manual dev/E2E use requires no DB recovery step.
close_reason: Shipped: PR #55 merged. Root-caused and reproduced directly against the real dev Postgres: loadConfig()'s test-mode DATABASE_URL/SESSION_SECRET were a soft fallback (env[name] ?? testValue) that let an ambient DATABASE_URL already exported in a developer/agent's shell (e.g. from a concurrently running npm run dev pointing at the real dev database) silently leak into npm run test, pointing resetDatabase()'s TRUNCATE at the real dev database instead of the isolated canvas_test one -- confirmed by exporting DATABASE_URL at the dev canvas DB and watching its user count drop from 3 to 0 on a test run, then confirming it stayed untouched after the fix. Two-layer fix: loadConfig() now hard-overrides databaseUrl/sessionSecret whenever NODE_ENV=test regardless of ambient env (CI's own unit-tests job already relied on exactly this fallback and never sets these vars itself, so no CI behavior change); resetDatabase() also gained a defense-in-depth guard querying current_database() and refusing to TRUNCATE anything not named *_test, in case a future code path bypasses loadConfig(). 5 new regression tests (179/179 total passing). Filed a separate low-priority follow-up (canvas-ai2) for an unrelated pre-existing testability quirk found while writing tests (requireEnv() ignores loadConfig's own env parameter).

title: Canvas never renders icon artwork for icon-shaped nodes (label text only)
description:
Selecting an icon from the Palette correctly creates a node with shape: 'icon' and an icon ref (apps/web/src/app/DiagramEditor.tsx:81-96, handleSelectIcon), but the interactive canvas never draws the actual icon graphic:

- apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx's renderNodeShape switch has no case 'icon' — it falls through to the generic default: a plain, sharp-cornered <rect>, same box as a plain 'rectangle'. This is the same pre-existing gap noted for 'cylinder'/'person' (data-model.md, feature 009 research.md §3 — explicitly out of scope for that feature).
- Neither Canvas.tsx nor shapes.tsx ever reads node.icon. Only the label text (the icon's display name, e.g. 'Lambda') is shown inside the box — no icon artwork is fetched or drawn.

By contrast, the export renderer already supports this correctly: packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts's renderNode (lines ~63-90) resolves node.icon via a resolveIcon callback and draws the real icon graphic inside the shape when exporting to SVG/PNG. So exports can show the true icon, but the canvas itself never can — what an architect sees while editing does not match what gets exported (a canvas/export fidelity gap, the same category of concern SC-004 elsewhere in this codebase cares about).

Fix needs: (1) a case 'icon' (or equivalent) rendering path in shapes.tsx that actually draws the icon artwork, not just a placeholder box, requiring the canvas to fetch/resolve icon assets the same way export does; (2) ideally also close the same gap for 'cylinder'/'person' while touching this switch, since they share the same silent-fallthrough defect.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a node via the icon palette shows the actual icon artwork on the canvas (not just label text in a generic box), matching what the SVG/PNG export already renders for the same node.
notes:
Follow-up 2026-07-31 (2): found and fixed a real bug via direct reproduction (started the actual
dev server + a throwaway Playwright script against it, not just guessing from CI logs) — icon
artwork never rendered for a node present AT MOUNT TIME (import, or a page reload), while one
added AFTER mount (a palette click on an already-settled canvas) worked fine. Root cause: a
separate `fetchedLibraries` ref marked a library as "already requested" synchronously before its
fetch resolved. Under React StrictMode's dev-only mount->cleanup->remount cycle: the first effect
instance marks the ref and starts fetching; its cleanup sets its own `cancelled` flag; the second
(surviving) instance sees the ref already marked and never fetches at all; the original response
arrives but is discarded. Only the very first mount is double-invoked, which is exactly why the
palette-click path (adds the node to an already-mounted, already-settled canvas) never hit this.
Fixed by gating "do I still need to fetch this?" on the cache itself (iconArtwork, now in the
effect's own dependency array) instead of a side-channel ref — neither StrictMode instance's
decision can suppress the other's fetch this way. Verified fixed by re-running the same
reproduction script against the live dev server after the change (confirmed via the rendered
node's actual HTML, not just an assumption).
This also means the e2e test that was failing in CI (icon-node-rendering.spec.ts's "preserves...
through save and reload", which hits the mount-time path via import) was catching a REAL bug, not
a flaky timing issue — the earlier 15s-timeout bump was a red herring fix that happened not to
help because the artwork genuinely never arrived, not because it arrived late. Left the longer
timeout in place regardless since it's a harmless safety margin, not the actual fix.
close_reason: Fixed canvas icon-artwork rendering, the export-side resolveIcon wiring gap discovered during investigation, the shape:'icon' round-trip bug, and cylinder's canvas rendering gap. Palette-preview thumbnails explicitly scoped out.

title: Edge arrowheads hidden: lines drawn to node center, nodes rendered on top
description:
Both edge renderers draw a straight line from the source node's center point to the target node's center point, with the arrowhead marker anchored at that endpoint — then render node shapes on top of the edge layer. Since the target node's opaque fill covers its own center, the arrowhead (and the portion of the line inside each node's bounding box) is completely hidden underneath the node. Visually this looks like a plain line with no arrow point, e.g. 'Sign Up --> Verify' in the Customer Onboarding diagram.

Affects both the interactive canvas and every export (SVG/PNG), since both use the same center-to-center endpoint calculation:
- apps/web/src/canvas/Canvas.tsx:510-530 (edges rendered before nodes at line 583; line endpoint 'to' is nodeCenter(target) at line 515)
- packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts:195-206 (renderEdge uses nodeCenter(target); edgeMarkup placed before nodeMarkup in renderToSvg)

Fix should clip each edge endpoint to the target (and probably source) node's shape boundary instead of its center, so the arrowhead lands in open space between the two shapes. Boundary calculation needs to account per-shape (rectangle vs circle vs diamond vs the 9 new shapes from feature 009 all differ), or at minimum a reasonable bounding-box intersection as a first pass.
acceptance_criteria: An edge between two nodes renders with a visible arrowhead in open space between the shapes, on both the canvas and SVG/PNG export, for at least rectangle/circle/diamond node shapes.
notes:
Fixed 2026-07-31: both renderers now clip each edge endpoint to the node's own shape boundary
instead of leaving it at the raw center. New shared helper `clipEdgeEndpoint` (exported from
packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts, same export-for-reuse pattern as
`splitLabelLines`) computes the boundary point along the line toward the other endpoint:
circle/double-circle use the true ellipse boundary, diamond its own rhombus boundary, and every
other shape (including all nine feature-009 shapes, icon/person/cylinder) falls back to a
rectangle bounding-box intersection — a reasonable approximation per this bead's own acceptance
criteria, not a claim of exact per-shape silhouette tracing. Endpoint is clamped so it never
extends past the other node's own center (near-overlapping nodes) or back past its own center
(degenerate zero-size case). Both apps/web/src/canvas/Canvas.tsx and
packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts call the identical shared function, so canvas and
export can never disagree (SC-004). Label midpoint position is unchanged (still center-to-center)
since only the visible line/arrowhead was the reported defect.
packages/diagram-core suite: 284 passing (was 280; +4 new via a new describe block in
render-svg.test.ts). apps/api: 119 passing + 1 skipped, unaffected. New e2e spec
(edge-arrowhead-visibility.spec.ts, 2 cases) added since this is a visually distinguishable
fix — not run this session (needs a live dev server + seeded E2E_PROJECT_ID).
close_reason: Edge endpoints now clip to node shape boundary (rectangle/circle+double-circle/diamond exact, rectangle-bbox fallback for other shapes) instead of raw center; arrowhead visible in both canvas and export.

title: Flaky in CI: project-switch unsaved-changes confirmation sometimes never appears
description:
apps/web/tests/e2e/project-visibility.spec.ts has two tests covering the unsaved-changes warning on project switch. In GitHub Actions, ONE of them fails per run and it alternates which:
  run 30457177512 - 'confirming a project switch...' timed out on getByTestId('confirm-project-switch')
  run 30457608394 - 'switching project with unsaved changes warns...' failed on expect(project-switch-confirm).toBeVisible()
Both mean the confirmation dialog never rendered. Run 30468263191 then passed with no code change, confirming it is intermittent rather than fixed.

The dialog is skipped when any of these hold in App.tsx requestProjectChange: nextProjectId === projectId, diagram is null, or hasUnsavedChanges is false. hasUnsavedChanges is computed in DiagramEditor.tsx and reported to App through an onUnsavedChangesChange prop inside a useEffect.

NOT YET DIAGNOSED. Ruled out so far:
  - useDslSync does not debounce; dsl is a synchronous useMemo over model, so it is not serialization lag
  - both tests already wait for [data-testid^='node-'] to reach count 1, and in the CI failures that assertion PASSED and the next line failed, so the edit had landed
  - could not reproduce locally: tests in isolation (3x), whole spec file (3x), --repeat-each=4 (44/44), GET /projects delayed 2.5s so the list lands after the editor opens, and CDP CPU throttling at 20x
Untested difference: CI seeds a fresh database (seeded project has 0 diagrams) whereas the local dev DB has ~1114, and CI runs all 97 tests across all spec files in one worker.
design: Key question to answer first: is this a TEST defect or a genuine product race? If a real user can switch project and silently lose unsaved work, the fix belongs in App.tsx/DiagramEditor.tsx, not the test. The parent-mirrors-child-state design (child useEffect -> parent useState -> read during an event handler) is the fragile part and may be worth replacing regardless of the outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with evidence from a CI trace, and the two tests pass across at least 10 consecutive CI runs without any assertion being weakened.
notes:
Fixed 2026-07-31 — root cause confirmed by direct code inspection, matching the working
hypothesis exactly: hasUnsavedChanges was a plain synchronous derived value in DiagramEditor.tsx
(dsl !== lastSavedDsl), but reached App.tsx only through a useEffect calling
onUnsavedChangesChange -> setHasUnsavedChanges — a real propagation lag (the parent's mirrored
state only lands on its NEXT passive-effect flush, one commit after the child's own DOM update).
requestProjectChange read the PARENT's mirrored state from closure; if the test's (or a real
user's) next action fired in the gap between the child's commit and the parent's own re-render,
hasUnsavedChanges was still stale `false` and the confirmation dialog never rendered.

Fix (per the bead's own DESIGN note): removed the mirrored parent state entirely.
DiagramEditor is now a forwardRef exposing a DiagramEditorHandle (`hasUnsavedChanges: () =>
boolean`) via useImperativeHandle — a plain getter closing over each render's current value, no
propagation delay since there is no second copy of the state. App.tsx reads
diagramEditorRef.current?.hasUnsavedChanges() synchronously at the moment of a project-switch
request instead of a useState value.

Verified against the actual running dev server (already up locally), not just unit/type checks:
wrote a throwaway Playwright script replicating the exact flaky test's steps (sign in, create a
second project, open a new flowchart, add a shape, wait for the node to render, then immediately
switch project) and ran it 15 times in a fresh browser context each time. All 15 showed the
confirmation dialog appearing reliably. Previously this depended on exact timing between the
child's DOM commit and the parent's passive-effect flush; the ref-based read has no such window
to race, so this isn't "got lucky 15 times" — the class of race is structurally gone.

packages/diagram-core: unaffected (frontend-only change). apps/api: unaffected. apps/web:
type-checks clean, no other references to the removed onUnsavedChangesChange prop remained.
close_reason: Removed the effect-mirrored parent state causing the race; App now reads DiagramEditor's unsaved-changes flag synchronously via a forwardRef/useImperativeHandle getter instead. Verified against the live dev server with 15 repeated runs of the exact flaky scenario, all passing.

title: A user with only a diagram-level share has no way to navigate to that diagram
description:
Feature 007 made project visibility access-controlled. A user who has been granted access to a single DIAGRAM, but not to its project, can no longer browse to it: the project browser needs project-level access, and there is no 'shared with me' list anywhere in the UI. The diagram is reachable only if someone sends them a direct link — and the editor has no per-diagram URL, so no such link exists.

Before 007 this worked, but only because any signed-in user could read any project's entire tree — i.e. the navigation path existed as a side effect of the access-control hole that 007 closed. Restoring the old behaviour is NOT the fix.

Surfaced by apps/web/tests/e2e/sharing.spec.ts, which navigates via the project browser to reach a diagram shared at view level. It passes today only because apps/api/src/seed/run.ts now also grants the architect project-level access to the seeded project — the seed masks the gap rather than the product solving it.
design: Two plausible directions: (a) a 'Shared with me' list on the home screen driven by share_grants where subject_type='diagram'; or (b) per-diagram deep links so a share can be delivered as a URL. (a) is self-contained; (b) is more broadly useful and would also let sharing.spec.ts navigate without any project grant.
acceptance_criteria: A user granted only a diagram-level share can reach and open that diagram through the UI, without holding any project-level access, and without being able to see any other diagram in that project.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-29. Confirmed with a live probe (temporary user, one diagram-level 'view' grant, no project access):
  GET /projects              -> {"projects":[]}  (so the UI shows the 'no projects yet' invitation)
  GET /diagrams/<shared>     -> 200               (the diagram is ALREADY fully readable)
  GET /projects/<owner>/tree -> 403               (correctly refused)
Probe data removed afterwards; dev DB back to 2 users.

Conclusion: access control is correct and needs no change. The defect is purely DISCOVERY — plus an actively misleading empty state that tells a user they have nothing when work is waiting.

Correction to this issue's original DESIGN field: (a) and (b) are NOT alternatives. Per-diagram deep links do not fix this bug — the recipient still needs someone to send them a link, and nothing tells them there is anything to ask for. (b) is a worthwhile separate change; (a) is the fix.

New risk identified for the spec: a 'shared with me' row that names the owning project would breach feature 007's FR-013a ('projects belonging to others MUST NOT be listed or named') while looking helpful. Needs an explicit decision.

Also noted: apps/api/src/seed/run.ts grants the architect project-level access, so sharing.spec.ts passes via the project browser and NO test currently covers the diagram-only case.

Brief prepared at docs/shared-diagram-access-brief.md. Routing through the full speckit cycle as feature 008.
close_reason: Implemented as feature 008 (specs/008-shared-diagram-access/). GET /shared-diagrams lists diagrams directly shared with the caller (one join over share_grants -> diagrams -> projects -> users, no access-resolution logic added). SharedDiagramsList renders on the home screen independent of project context, omitted entirely when empty; the false 'no projects' invitation is suppressed once a share exists. Row shows project name as inert text (feature 007 FR-013a explicitly carved out for this one disclosure, never an ancestor project) and who shared it. All 24 tasks in tasks.md complete; full suite green: 154 diagram-core, 119+1 skipped api (+7 new), 102+1 skipped e2e (+6 new). No pre-existing assertion weakened.

title: Flaky e2e test: standards-metadata.spec.ts count() races the async history render
description:
Surfaced by a real CI failure on PR #128 (canvas-ljx-fastify-vuln-floor, run 34625671957, job
103350205441) -- 'every standard in the list is identifiable by name, including pre-existing
ones' failed with count === 0. Confirmed NOT a regression from that PR (its only diff was a
package.json/package-lock.json semver-range string, zero functional change) by observing the
identical underlying app code (main after canvas-80m + canvas-v4u) had just passed the full e2e
suite cleanly minutes earlier on canvas-v4u's own direct merge-to-main run.

Root cause (confirmed via the CI failure artifact's page snapshot, captured moments after the
assertion failed): the test's `rows.count()` on `[data-testid^="standard-row-"]` is a single-shot
read taken immediately after `openStandardsAdmin(page)` returns, which only waits for the
create-publish-standard button to become visible -- not for the standards-history list's own
separate async fetch/render. The failure snapshot shows the history list DID contain 3 real
items with real data by the time it was captured, confirming this was a pure timing race, not a
real "no data" bug -- StandardsEditor.tsx does correctly render `data-testid="standard-row-*"` on
every history item.

Same class of bug as canvas-mup (style-affordance.spec.ts's "clicking Clear" test), fixed there
via expect.poll() instead of a single-shot read.
design: Replaced the single-shot count() with expect.poll(() => rows.count()).toBeGreaterThan(0) before reading count for the loop bound, matching canvas-mup's own established fix pattern exactly. Checked the file's other 4 tests for the same single-shot-read-after-page-load pattern -- none have it (every other assertion is a Playwright locator assertion that auto-retries on its own).
acceptance_criteria: The test no longer fails when the standards-history fetch resolves slightly late. Verified by running the full spec file 5 times in a row locally against the real app -- 5/5 passing every time.
close_reason: Fixed via expect.poll(() => rows.count()).toBeGreaterThan(0), matching canvas-mup's precedent. Verified: full spec file run 5x locally against the real app, 5/5 passing every time. eslint clean.
