title: Keycloak SSO e2e spec (sso-login.spec.ts) never runs in CI
description:
apps/web/tests/e2e/sso-login.spec.ts (canvas-mi9) drives a real Keycloak login, including live
TOTP/MFA enrollment, through Keycloak's actual login theme -- not a mock. It's gated behind
E2E_SSO_READY=1, which requires a running local Keycloak (docker compose --profile sso) with the
API server started with OIDC_ISSUER_URL/CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/REDIRECT_URI pointed at it (see
RUNBOOK.md's "Keycloak SSO" section) -- not part of the default `npm run dev` flow every other
spec assumes.

Confirmed still true by reading .github/workflows/ci.yml's e2e-tests job end to end: it installs
Playwright browsers, seeds E2E_PROJECT_ID, and runs `npx playwright test` via the Vite dev
server's own webServer config -- there is no Keycloak service, no `--profile sso` compose
invocation, and E2E_SSO_READY is never set. So sso-login.spec.ts's own test.skip guard
(SSO_READY = process.env.E2E_SSO_READY === '1') always short-circuits it in CI, exactly as its own
comment discloses ("Not run in CI today ... standing up Keycloak there is tracked separately, not
a blocker for shipping the SSO integration itself") -- but no bead tracking that follow-up
actually existed until now.

Net effect: the SSO login flow (including MFA enrollment) has zero automated regression coverage
in CI. It has been verified live against a real deployed Keycloak by hand (canvas-mi9's own
implementation, and canvas-252/canvas-252.1's logout work), but any future regression in
oidc.ts/LoginForm.tsx's SSO path would only be caught by another manual pass, not CI.
acceptance_criteria:
A decision is made and acted on (either is an acceptable close): either (a) CI's e2e-tests job
gains a Keycloak service (docker compose --profile sso, matching local dev) plus realm
provisioning and E2E_SSO_READY=1/OIDC_* env wiring so sso-login.spec.ts actually runs and passes
in CI, or (b) the tradeoff (extra CI time/complexity for standing up a full IdP vs. the coverage
gap) is deliberately evaluated and the decision to keep it manual-only is confirmed and documented
(e.g. in RUNBOOK.md or the spec's own comment) rather than left as an unexamined gap.
close_reason: Added a 'Start Keycloak' + 'Wait for Keycloak' step pair to CI's e2e-tests job (.github/workflows/ci.yml), bringing up the same docker-compose.yml keycloak service (--profile sso) used for local dev, with the same OIDC_*/E2E_SSO_READY env values RUNBOOK.md documents. sso-login.spec.ts now runs in CI instead of always skipping. Verified locally end-to-end mirroring the exact new CI steps (fresh Keycloak, seed, wait, API server with OIDC configured, playwright test) -- both tests pass. Pushed via the GitHub MCP push_files tool since the local gh CLI OAuth token lacks the workflow scope needed to push .github/workflows/* changes directly (now documented in RUNBOOK.md's own 'Pushing to .github/workflows/*' section, which already existed and confirmed this as the right path). PR #127, squash-auto-merge enabled.

title: Route-level request validation is inconsistent (hand-rolled checks, no declarative schema)
description:
Verified live by surveying every apps/api/src/**/*.routes.ts file (17 total): 14 use hand-rolled imperative validation (a manual 'if (!field) { reply.code(400).send(...) }' per required field, e.g. import.routes.ts's 'if (!name || !dslContent)') -- zero use Fastify's own declarative 'schema:' route option, and zero import zod directly. The only zod usage anywhere in apps/api is ai/diagram-tools.ts (the AI tool-calling layer, validating LLM tool-call arguments per the Vercel AI SDK's own convention) -- a completely different subsystem from HTTP route request validation. The 3 route files with no manual-check hit (diagram-type.routes.ts, idp-proxy.routes.ts, docs/api-docs.routes.ts) simply have no request body to validate at all, not a better validation approach -- so the real split is 14/14 hand-rolled among routes that validate anything.

This was first disclosed in docs/solution-architecture-document.md's own Known Limitations section (canvas-lfc's OpenAPI work surfaced it) and is now confirmed current, not stale.
acceptance_criteria: Routes that accept a request body validate it declaratively (Fastify's own 'schema' option, or zod via a shared @fastify/zod-style adapter) instead of ad hoc imperative checks -- consistent error shape/status code across all 14 currently-hand-rolled routes, and (as a natural side effect, shared implementation vehicle with canvas-lfc) those same schemas feed /docs' request-body documentation instead of needing separate annotation.
notes: Closely related to canvas-lfc (OpenAPI route schema enrichment) -- adding a Fastify 'schema' option per route is the same mechanical change that fixes both the documentation gap and this validation-consistency gap at once. Filed as its own bead since canvas-lfc's stated acceptance criteria is framed around documentation richness specifically, not validation consistency.
close_reason: Converted all 17 hand-rolled imperative validation checks across 11 route files (admin.routes.ts, user-lookup.routes.ts, ai-settings.routes.ts, diagram-chat.routes.ts, diagram.routes.ts x5, import.routes.ts, import-template.routes.ts, export.routes.ts, library.routes.ts, project.routes.ts x2, sharing.routes.ts x2) to Fastify's declarative JSON-Schema 'schema' route option. Also disabled Fastify's default AJV coerceTypes (app.ts) since it was silently coercing wrongly-typed values (e.g. a JSON number) into the schema's declared type instead of rejecting them, caught by a real pre-existing test failure (diagram-description.test.ts's 'rejects a non-string description with 400') during verification. All error responses flow through the existing global setErrorHandler unchanged, same {error} shape/status codes as before. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, full apps/api suite green (362/362 + 1 skipped perf test), eslint clean on all touched files, and live-confirmed /docs/json now shows enriched request-body/querystring schemas for the converted routes.

title: Enrich OpenAPI route schemas for richer Swagger docs (request/response bodies, tags)
description: The OpenAPI/Swagger wiring (apps/api/src/docs/api-docs.routes.ts, gated behind ENABLE_API_DOCS) lists every real route (Fastify's own introspection needs no per-route schema for that), but request/response bodies, params, and tags stay undocumented until individual routes opt into Fastify's schema option. Adding that across all ~16 *.routes.ts files' worth of endpoints (47 total) is a much larger, separate pass than the foundational wiring itself -- deliberately not attempted in that pass.
acceptance_criteria: A meaningful subset (or all) of the 47 routes gain a Fastify schema (body/params/querystring/response, tags grouping by resource) so /docs shows real, browsable request/response shapes instead of just path+method. Each route's schema.security should reference the existing cookieAuth scheme where the route actually requires auth (most of them).
notes: Foundational wiring (this session): apps/api/src/docs/api-docs.routes.ts, config.ts's enableApiDocs, app.ts's early registration. Verified live: /docs/json correctly lists all 47 routes.
close_reason: Tags + security done for all 62 registered operations (recount at fix time -- grew from the bead's original 47), the scope explicitly chosen for this pass. Added a top-level 'tags' array to the OpenAPI document (api-docs.routes.ts, 12 tags grouped by resource: Auth, Health, Projects, Diagrams, DiagramTypes, Export, Sharing, Standards, Libraries, AI, Admin, Users -- Users split out of admin/user-lookup.routes.ts since it is not actually admin-gated) and a schema.tags/schema.security entry to every route registration across all 18 route files (auth/local.ts, auth/oidc.ts, auth/session.ts, app.ts's /health, and all 15 *.routes.ts files). security is [{cookieAuth:[]}] wherever a preHandler chain actually enforces auth (requireAuth/requireRole/requireDiagramAccess/requireProjectAccess/requireDiagramOwnerOrAdmin/requireProjectOwnerOrAdmin -- confirmed by reading access-control.middleware.ts, all of which check request.session.user themselves) and an explicit security: [] (not merely omitted) for the 6 genuinely public auth routes (login, config, OIDC login/callback, logout, me) plus /health -- explicit so /docs shows these were deliberately reviewed as public, not just never annotated. Live-verified against a running server's /docs/json: all 62 operations have both tags and an explicit security key, 0 missing either. Full apps/api suite green (362/362 +1 skipped), tsc clean, eslint clean (0 errors, 1 pre-existing unrelated warning). Request/response body schemas remain only partially filled in (canvas-80m's spillover covers 17 checks) -- filed as a dedicated follow-up (canvas-62y) rather than silently left as an unexamined gap, since it's a substantially larger lift than this pass's mechanical tags/security work.

title: C4 Context node labels can overflow vertically when a long label wraps to multiple lines
description: Found while investigating canvas-4lu (which turned out to be a different, unrelated bug -- see that bead's history): plain-shape DiagramNodes (no icon, no attribute/member table -- includes C4's 'person'/'cylinder' shapes among every other plain shape) fell back to a fixed DEFAULT_NODE_SIZE (140x60) regardless of label length. A too-wide label already wrapped to fit the box's WIDTH (canvas-3zb's labelMaxWidth), but nothing grew the box's HEIGHT to fit however many lines that wrapping produced, so a label wrapping to 3+ lines rendered past the shape's own bottom edge -- a real, separate, still-latent bug confirmed by code reading (not by live screenshot -- unlike canvas-4lu's actual reported symptom, no live repro was done for this one).

notes: Already implemented and tested in this same session: packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts's new plainNodeSize() (mirrors iconNodeSize's own fixed-width/grows-height-with-line-count precedent, canvas-23t.5), wired into nodeSize()'s fallback; apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx's own nodeSize() calls the same function. 911/911 packages/diagram-core tests passing (13 new cases), eslint/tsc clean. Closing immediately -- this is a real fix already verified via automated tests, just not the fix canvas-4lu's actual report needed.
close_reason: Implemented and tested earlier in this same session (plainNodeSize in svg-renderer.ts, wired into both renderers' nodeSize()). 911/911 diagram-core tests passing, eslint/tsc clean. Filed retroactively to properly separate this real-but-different fix from canvas-4lu, whose actual reported bug turned out to be the Add Shape toolbar's SHAPE_GLYPHS map (Canvas.tsx), not diagram-node rendering at all -- confirmed via a live screenshot after the initial diagnosis (this bead's own fix) turned out not to be what canvas-4lu needed.

title: deploy.sh's own printed canvas-keycloak-users invocation doesn't work as documented
description: Two real gaps found during a live first-ever canvas Azure deploy (2026-09-08): (1) deploy.sh's confirmation prompt (read -r -p "Proceed with deployment? [y/N]") aborts silently with exit 1 when run non-interactively/no stdin -- no error explaining why, just 'Aborted.'. (2) The exact invocation deploy.sh prints at the end for provisioning real users -- 'az containerapp job start --name canvas-keycloak-users --resource-group canvas-rg --env-vars KC_USERS=...' -- fails on the installed az CLI/containerapp extension version: passing --env-vars without --image/--command/--args causes the CLI to require a full container override, which drops the job's own command/args (node infra/keycloak/create-users.mjs), so the container instead boots the API server's default entrypoint and crashes on a missing DATABASE_URL. Worked around live by also passing --image/--command/--args and the job's other original env vars (KEYCLOAK_URL/KEYCLOAK_REALM/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME/KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD via secretref:) alongside KC_USERS.
acceptance_criteria: deploy.sh's own printed post-deploy instructions for canvas-keycloak-users (and ideally canvas-seed/canvas-migrate too, if they'd hit the same gap) actually work when copy-pasted verbatim on a current az CLI/containerapp extension. Confirmation prompt either accepts a --yes/non-interactive flag or documents the workaround.
notes: Live deploy this session: canvas-rg fully provisioned (23 resources), API/frontend health-checked 200, canvas-migrate succeeded, one real architect user (muir.jc@gmail.com) created successfully via the worked-around invocation.

title: Canvas UI: drag a container into another container to nest it (parentContainerId), cross-family
description: Discovered while closing jmuir-dtu.19 (architecture nested groups): Canvas.tsx has ZERO references to parentContainerId anywhere -- there is no drag/drop or any other UI mechanism to nest one container inside another for ANY diagram family (flowchart subgraphs, C4 boundaries, UML namespaces, architecture groups all support parentContainerId in the model/DSL, all can only ever get it via hand-edited DSL or import today). This is broader than architecture-specific: it's a generic canvas-container-interaction gap. The backing ops already exist and are already tested (setContainerParent/removeContainerParent, diagram-ops.ts, added in canvas-2s6.1) -- this bead is UI wiring only: detect a container being dragged and dropped onto/inside another container's bounds (mirrors the existing node-dragged-into-container detection moveContainer's own drag handling already does, generalized one level up to container-into-container), call setContainerParent on drop, and removeContainerParent when dragged back out to open canvas. Needs a sensible visual affordance (e.g. the target container highlighting on drag-over, matching how a node-drop-target might already highlight if that exists) and needs to interact correctly with moveContainer's own existing descendant-cascade logic (a container being nested must not create a cycle -- setContainerParent already guards against direct self-nesting but not deeper cycles, per its own doc comment).
acceptance_criteria: A user can drag one container onto/into another container on the canvas and it becomes nested (parentContainerId set), for at least flowchart and architecture (the two families with the clearest visual nesting semantics today). Dragging a nested container back out to open canvas clears the nesting. New Playwright e2e coverage. No regression to existing container drag/move/resize behavior (containers.spec.ts stays green).
close_reason: Canvas UI: drag a container into another to nest it, cross-family (all 6 families, exceeding the bead's own minimum flowchart+architecture scope -- C4/UML nesting is equally valid in their own DSL grammar, ERD has no container concept to nest at all so the surface is a harmless no-op there, and sequence containers are already drag-disabled entirely per FR-013/canvas-7vs.1's computed-only-layout guard, so no family-gating was needed at all). handlePointerUp gained a new 'container' branch (mirrored the existing node-into-container drop-resolution pattern one level up): resolves the dragged container's own centre point against every OTHER container's bounds (via containerAtPoint, now taking an optional excludeIds set) and calls setContainerParent on a hit, removeContainerParent when dropped on open canvas. A live green (#16a34a) drop-target highlight (new containerDropTargetId state, updated every pointer-move during a container drag, resolved/cleared on drop) shows which container it would nest into before release. A new descendantContainerIds helper (mirrors moveContainer's own descendant-collection loop) excludes the dragged container and all its own descendants from drop-target candidacy, so dropping a parent onto/over a child it's carrying along can never register as a nesting target. title: Implement flowchart click href/tooltip node interactions (grouping G)
description: The last open item under jmuir-dzd -- a deliberately deferred (not missed) gap, with its design already fully decided during jmuir-dzd's own discussion (see bd show jmuir-dzd notes). Implement AS DECIDED: href/tooltip form only (click <id> href "<url>" ["<tooltip>"] [_blank]). The callback form (click <id> call fn()) is a SECURITY REJECTION, not a deferral -- must produce a clear, named parse error, never silent tolerance or execution. New DiagramNode.link?: { href: string; tooltip?: string; target?: '_blank' } model field, parser directive, serializer. MANDATORY: href must be scheme-allowlisted (http(s):// or a relative path only) and XML-escaped on export, or click A href "javascript:..." becomes a stored XSS payload the moment the diagram is opened. Export renderer wraps the node's shape+label in a real SVG <a>. Canvas UI: a link popup mirroring the existing style-popup pattern to set/clear href+tooltip on a node. Route through appsec-expert review before merge given the disclosed XSS risk.
acceptance_criteria: click <id> href "https://..." ["tooltip"] parses, round-trips, and exports as a real clickable SVG <a> with scheme-allowlisted, XML-escaped output. click <id> call fn() produces a named rejection error, never executes or silently drops. A canvas UI popup can set/clear the link. Explicit XSS-payload test (javascript: scheme) proves rejection/neutralization. appsec-expert reviewed before merge.
close_reason: Flowchart click href/tooltip node interactions (grouping G), implemented exactly as decided (bd show jmuir-dzd's own notes): href/tooltip form only. New DiagramNode.link (href/tooltip/target) model field + shared isAllowedLinkHref() scheme-allowlist check (http(s)/relative only). Parser: CLICK_HREF_DIRECTIVE parses the real form; CLICK_CALL_DIRECTIVE explicitly REJECTS 'click <id> call fn()' with a clean, named parse error (never silently dropped or executed) -- checked before href so no call variant can slip through as something else. An href with a disallowed scheme is also a hard parse error, not silent tolerance. Serializer re-emits a real 'click <id> href ...' line (native Mermaid grammar, not front-matter, matching subgraph direction's own precedent) -- applied as a second pass, and a node referencing an undeclared id is silently skipped (style directive's own established precedent, not an FR-003 violation). SVG export renderer wraps the node's shape+label in a real <a href> (with a <title> child for the tooltip), re-validating isAllowedLinkHref independently as defense in depth since link is also settable directly via diagram-ops.ts. New setNodeLink op (throws on a disallowed scheme, mirroring updateNodeLabel's own empty-label precedent) backs a new flowchart-only canvas UI popup (LinkPopup, opened via a new per-node Link affordance) that sets/clears href+tooltip+target, with client-side validation before ever calling the throwing op. Routed through appsec-expert review before merge per the bead's own explicit requirement given the disclosed XSS risk -- the FIRST pass came back 'DO NOT MERGE' with two real, live, verified bypasses: (1) isAllowedLinkHref's original hand-rolled regex missed a leading-whitespace/control-character scheme obfuscation (' javascript:...' matched no scheme prefix at all under the regex, so was wrongly treated as a safe relative path, while the WHATWG URL Standard every real browser implements strips that same leading whitespace before scheme detection -- fixed by delegating to the platform's own URL parser (new URL(href, base).protocol) instead of re-implementing its normalization by hand); (2) unescaped '"'/newline characters in href/tooltip could break out of the DSL's own unescapable '"..."' click-href token and inject a second, independent 'click <otherNodeId> href ...' line targeting an unrelated node whose own href was never validated -- fixed by rejecting (not escaping, since the DSL grammar has no escape syntax to produce) any href/tooltip containing a quote or line break, enforced at setNodeLink, defensively re-checked in serializeClickHref (which now treats a violation as 'no link' rather than ever emitting broken/injectable DSL), and in the canvas popup's own client-side validation. Also fixed, as recommended hardening: apps/api's export route now sends Content-Disposition: attachment (a fixed, non-diagram-derived filename, so the fix itself can't become a new header-injection surface) on all three export formats, since a direct GET with no download-forcing header would otherwise render the SVG inline at the API's own origin, widening any XSS-class bug's blast radius. The reviewer re-verified the fixed code independently (re-ran every original bypass payload against the corrected functions, ran the full diagram-core/apps/api suites themselves) and gave explicit sign-off to merge. Also fixed a small cosmetic gap the reviewer noted in passing: the parse-error message for a disallowed scheme now names the real scheme (reusing the same URL-parser resolution) instead of falling back to a generic '(unknown)' for an obfuscated href. New test coverage across every layer: flowchart-click-href.test.ts (29 tests: parse/serialize/round-trip, the call() rejection, the full scheme-allowlist including every bypass class, isAllowedLinkHref unit tests, and the serializer's own defensive-omission cases for a maliciously-direct model), render-svg.test.ts (10 new tests: <a>/<title> wrapping, target, XML-escaping including the literal double-quote/script-tag PoC, and the export-boundary re-check for both a plain and an obfuscated disallowed scheme), diagram-ops.test.ts (11 new tests for setNodeLink including the quote/newline rejection cases), apps/api diagrams.test.ts (Content-Disposition assertions on all 3 formats), and a new e2e spec (flowchart-click-link.spec.ts, 12 tests: affordance visibility per family, full set/edit/clear/reopen/Escape flows, and 3 dedicated client-side-rejection tests for the javascript:/data:/leading-space/quote-injection cases). Verification: packages/diagram-core 859/859 (up from 849 after the appsec fixes), apps/api 333/333 (+1 skipped), tsc --noEmit and eslint clean across api/web/diagram-core, e2e spec 12/12 plus prior regression subsets (style-affordance/c4-element-kind-authoring/fields-affordance/label-affordance, 36 tests) all green. title: sast-bearer flags TEST_SESSION_SECRET/TEST_DATABASE_URL as hardcoded secrets (CWE-798) on every PR
description:
The sast-bearer CI check has failed with 2 CRITICAL findings on every recent PR (confirmed on both #85 and #86, neither of which touches the flagged file) -- a long-standing false positive, not a real vulnerability:

  CRITICAL: Usage of hard-coded secret [CWE-798]
  File: apps/api/src/config.ts:67
   67 const TEST_SESSION_SECRET = 'test-secret-at-least-32-characters-long';

  CRITICAL: Usage of hard-coded secret [CWE-798]
  File: apps/api/src/config.ts:87
   87     sessionSecret: isTest ? TEST_SESSION_SECRET : requireEnv('SESSION_SECRET'),

TEST_SESSION_SECRET (and its sibling TEST_DATABASE_URL, same file) are deliberate, non-sensitive test-only fixtures -- canvas-uw8's own comment on this code explains they're a hard override specifically so NODE_ENV=test can never accidentally pick up a real ambient DATABASE_URL/SESSION_SECRET from a developer's shell. Production always requires the real env vars via requireEnv(), which throws if unset. Bearer's static heuristic just pattern-matches 'string literal assigned to a *SECRET*-named variable' with no awareness that this one is gated behind isTest and grants no access to anything real.

Not currently merge-blocking (main has no branch protection requiring sast-bearer, confirmed via the API; PR #85 merged today with this exact same failure) -- filed as housekeeping so the check stops showing red on every single PR, not because it's blocking anything today.
acceptance_criteria: sast-bearer passes cleanly on a fresh PR that doesn't touch config.ts. Two reasonable approaches to evaluate: (1) bearer ignore add f97fd904cba0a080f088fde91b7534fc_0 / _1 (or regenerate the ignore-list, since these fingerprints may be content-derived and could change if the file is edited) via bearer's own suppression file, with a comment explaining why; (2) restructure the constant so Bearer's heuristic doesn't trip at all (e.g. read it through a small helper function rather than a bare top-level const, or derive it non-literally) -- prefer whichever this repo's own security-tooling conventions already establish elsewhere, if any precedent exists.
notes: Bearer version at time of finding: v0.48.4. Confirmed via job logs on both PR #85 (https://github.com/muirjc/canvas/pull/85) and PR #86 (https://github.com/muirjc/canvas/pull/86) -- identical 2 findings, identical file/lines, on runs that never touched config.ts, confirming this is unconditional/pre-existing rather than triggered by any particular diff.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #90 (auto-merge enabled): added bearer.ignore with the two false-positive CWE-798 fingerprints (TEST_SESSION_SECRET/TEST_DATABASE_URL, config.ts), generated via the real bearer CLI against a live full-repo scan matching CI's exact invocation, each with an explanatory comment. Verified locally: full-repo scan went from 2 CRITICAL findings to 'no failures were detected'.

title: ER: quoted relationship labels kept literal quote marks; attribute inline comments discarded
description:
Found via a deliberate closer/more-skeptical re-audit of erd.ts, following the two real bugs (canvas-x66 missing attribute rendering, canvas-2ut discarded cardinality) the user found by direct testing. Two more real, verifiable defects in the same file:

1. Quoted relationship labels keep their literal quote characters. Real Mermaid allows a relationship label to be quoted (e.g. CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : "places, urgently"), needed if the label contains a comma or just written that way -- but RELATIONSHIP_PATTERN's label capture group is a raw greedy .+, and nothing ever stripped the surrounding quotes. So the rendered/exported label showed the literal quote marks around the text. Confirmed against this codebase's own established convention elsewhere for exactly this situation: c4.ts's POSITIONAL_MACRO_ARG regex (/^"([^"]*)"$/) strips quotes from a quoted macro argument the same way -- erd.ts was the one family-parser inconsistent with that precedent.

2. Attribute inline comments (string id PK "the primary key" -- real, documented Mermaid syntax; per Mermaid's own docs this metadata "does not impact the rendering of the diagram" but is still real authored content) were parsed by ATTRIBUTE_LINE's own 4th capture group and then immediately discarded -- EntityAttribute had no field to hold it. There was an existing test ('does not fail on a trailing quoted comment') that explicitly asserted the comment vanishes, treating not-crashing as success rather than checking the comment survives -- a documented-by-omission gap, not caught before now.
acceptance_criteria: (1) A relationship label that is a single quoted span start-to-end has its surrounding quotes stripped on parse; a label with an internal, non-wrapping quote, or no quotes at all, is left exactly as written -- no regression. (2) EntityAttribute gains an optional comment field; the parser captures it and the serializer re-emits it as a trailing quoted string, round-tripping exactly through export/re-import. Neither renderer needs to draw the comment (matches Mermaid's own non-rendering treatment) -- round-trip fidelity only, per this codebase's FR-003 no-silent-drop principle.
notes: CORRECTION (found live, immediately after this bead was closed): the acceptance criteria's claim that 'neither renderer needs to draw the comment (matches Mermaid's own non-rendering treatment)' was WRONG -- verified against Mermaid's own erRenderer.js source that attribute comments DO render, as their own rightmost column after type/name/key. User reported live: a real diagram with comments on several attributes showed none of them on the canvas. Fixed in packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts's formatAttributeRow (canvas-x66's shared table-rendering function, so both the export renderer and the interactive canvas picked up the fix automatically via the existing tableNodeLayout sharing -- no separate Canvas.tsx/shapes.tsx change needed). New test in render-svg.test.ts. 563/563 diagram-core tests passing.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in the same session it was found — see notes for details. 562/562 diagram-core tests passing (4 new).

title: DiagramContainer.role never visually distinguishes loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/note/box/namespace/activate/deactivate
description: Every container role -- a C4 System_Boundary, a sequence loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break, a sequence note-left/note-right/note-over, a sequence box grouping, a sequence activate/deactivate marker, or a UML namespace/note -- renders as the exact same generic dashed gray box with a corner label. Confirmed: renderContainer (svg-renderer.ts) never reads container.role at all; Canvas.tsx's own container-rendering comment says so explicitly ('Appearance is deliberately unchanged from what the export renderer draws -- this feature adds interaction, not styling').
acceptance_criteria: Not fully specified -- needs design judgment on which roles most need visual distinction and how (e.g. loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break could get distinct label prefixes or corner-tab styling like real Mermaid; note-* could get a different fill/border; activate/deactivate are point-in-time markers, not boxes, and may need an entirely different geometry -- a vertical bar segment, not a rectangle -- which likely depends on canvas-7vs's sequence-lifeline child being addressed first). Namespace/C4-boundary distinction is more cosmetic and lower priority than the sequence roles.
notes:
The sequence-specific roles (loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break/note-*/box/activate/deactivate) are effectively blocked on / best addressed alongside canvas-7vs's sequence-lifeline child, since activate/deactivate in particular has no sensible rendering without real lifeline geometry to anchor to. UML namespace/note and C4 boundaries are independent and could be picked up separately/sooner if desired.
canvas-7vs.1 (sequence lifeline/timeline rendering) is now implemented and closed -- the real geometry (participant lifelines, message/activation/block rows, note/box positions) this bead's sequence-specific roles depend on now exists (specs/011-sequence-lifeline-rendering/). Unblocked, not resolved -- container.role still renders as the same generic dashed box for every role; this bead's own scope (distinct visual style per role) remains open.
Implemented 2026-09-06: new containerRoleStyle(role) shared between svg-renderer.ts (both the generic renderContainer and the sequence-specific renderSequenceBlock) and Canvas.tsx's own generic container JSX (SC-004 parity). Sequence/UML notes: pale-yellow solid-bordered box. Sequence box: finer dash (2,3) than a control-flow block. UML namespace: filled header band. Sequence loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break (not rect, which keeps the plain default -- its identity is fill color, canvas-7vs.2): indigo stroke (#5b6b8c) + corner-tab rect behind the role+label text, mirroring real Mermaid's folded-corner convention. activate/deactivate needed no further work -- 011's bar rendering already gives them distinct geometry. Deliberately NOT covered: C4 boundary kinds and flowchart subgraphs (both role: undefined) -- C4's gap is real but a parser/model issue, not a renderer one (boundary keyword was never captured at all); filed as jmuir-dtu's own child (canvas-7vs.11), reparented out of this epic since it doesn't fit 'renderer completeness'. diagram-core 662/662 (+6 new render-svg.test.ts cases); apps/web E2E 10/10 new sequence-rendering.spec.ts cases + 53-test regression subset green.
close_reason: Every container role now gets a distinct default fill/stroke/border via a shared containerRoleStyle(), applied identically in both renderers. C4 boundary-kind distinction and flowchart subgraphs deliberately excluded (see notes) -- C4 gap filed separately as jmuir-dtu's canvas-7vs.11.

title: Architecture {group} edge modifier (sourceIsGroup/targetIsGroup) never escalates edge to group boundary
description: DiagramEdge.sourceIsGroup/targetIsGroup (architecture diagrams' {group} edge modifier, e.g. serviceId{group}:T --> B:otherServiceId{group}) are parsed and modeled correctly (jmuir-dtu.5) -- the field's own doc comment in diagram-model.ts explicitly frames it as inherently visual: "escalating this endpoint's connection point to the service's parent group boundary... a purely visual escalation hint." But neither renderer reads it at all -- edges always terminate at the individual node's own boundary (nodeCenter/clipEdgeEndpoint), never at a group/container boundary, regardless of the {group} modifier.
acceptance_criteria: When set, that endpoint's edge line terminates at the boundary of the service's PARENT CONTAINER (the group), not the service node itself -- likely needs the edge-rendering code to look up the node's containerId and use the container's bounding box instead of the node's own for that endpoint's clip calculation. Both renderers must agree (SC-004).
notes: An edge with neither flag set renders exactly as today. Depends on knowing a node's parent container's rendered bounds at edge-draw time -- check whether containerSize/container position lookups are already plumbed through to renderEdge/the Canvas.tsx edge-drawing code, or need adding.
close_reason: Fixed: {group} (sourceIsGroup/targetIsGroup) now escalates the clip box to the parent container's boundary (architectureEndpointBox, shared by both renderers) instead of the service node's own. Verified live: edge line correctly terminates at the group container's computed boundary (340,140), not the service node's own box. Bundled with canvas-7vs.6 per the fix plan (same edge-endpoint-resolution code). 605/605 diagram-core tests passing.

title: Architecture edge anchor hints (sourceAnchor/targetAnchor: T/B/L/R) ignored by both renderers
description: DiagramEdge.sourceAnchor/targetAnchor (architecture diagrams' explicit :T/:B/:L/:R connection-side hint, e.g. serviceId:T --> B:otherServiceId) are parsed and modeled correctly but neither renderer reads them -- edges are always clipped to the node's shape boundary toward the OTHER node's center (clipEdgeEndpoint, svg-renderer.ts), regardless of which side the DSL explicitly named. Confirmed zero occurrences of sourceAnchor/targetAnchor outside architecture.ts's own parse/serialize code.
acceptance_criteria: When set, an anchor hint pins that endpoint to the actual named side of the node's bounding box (top/bottom/left/right midpoint) rather than the nearest-point-toward-the-other-node default clipEdgeEndpoint currently always computes. Both renderers must agree (SC-004).
notes: An edge with no anchor hints set (every non-architecture edge, or an architecture edge that didn't specify one) keeps today's clipEdgeEndpoint behavior exactly.
close_reason: Fixed: an explicit :T/:B/:L/:R anchor hint now pins that endpoint to the literal side's midpoint (clipToAnchorSide, svg-renderer.ts, shared by Canvas.tsx) instead of the direction-toward-the-other-node default. Verified live against real anchor-hint architecture examples. 605/605 diagram-core tests passing.

title: UML stereotype (<<Interface>> etc) never rendered
description: DiagramNode.umlStereotype (a <<Stereotype>> annotation, e.g. Interface/Abstract/Service/Enumeration/any custom word) is parsed and modeled correctly (jmuir-dtu.2) and IS emitted back out on serialize (uml.ts: annotationPart = node.umlStereotype ? ` <<${node.umlStereotype}>> ` : ''), but neither renderer ever reads it -- a class's header in both renderers is plain node.label with no stereotype decoration at all.

Easier than it would have been pre-canvas-x66 -- the table-body header band that fix introduced (tableNodeLayout in svg-renderer.ts) is exactly where this belongs; likely just needs a second line/row in the header, sized into tableNodeSize's existing height calculation.

close_reason: Fixed: umlStereotype now renders as its own smaller line stacked above the class name in the shared table header (svg-renderer.ts's tableNodeLayout/tableNodeSize, mirrored in Canvas.tsx). No change for a class with no stereotype. 574/574 diagram-core tests passing (3 new).

title: UML relationship cardinality labels (sourceCardinality/targetCardinality) never rendered
description: DiagramEdge.sourceCardinality/targetCardinality (the quoted multiplicity label at each end of a UML relationship, e.g. "1", "0..1", "*", "1..*") are parsed and modeled correctly (jmuir-dtu.2) but never drawn near the edge endpoints in either renderer -- only edge.label (the relationship's own name, if any) is drawn, at the edge's midpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Each of sourceCardinality/targetCardinality, when set, renders as small text near its respective endpoint (offset from the node boundary along the edge, not overlapping the node itself), in both renderers, matching real Mermaid's own rendering convention for class-diagram multiplicity labels.

title: Login shows raw "Not Found" when local password auth is disabled
description: On the Azure deployment, ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH defaults to false (canvas-ycu.1), so POST /auth/local/login (apps/api/src/auth/local.ts, gated in app.ts:69-71) is never registered. Submitting the login form then hits Fastify's default 404 handler, whose JSON body is {error: "Not Found", ...}. LoginForm.tsx surfaces body.error verbatim (via api.ts's request()), so a user attempting email/password sign-in on an SSO-only deployment sees the bare, confusing string "Not Found" instead of a message explaining that password sign-in is disabled and they should use SSO. Found live: user reported exactly this on the deployed instance.
acceptance_criteria: When ALLOW_LOCAL_AUTH is false, the login form either hides the email/password fields entirely (oidcEnabled is already fetched via GET /auth/config, which is unconditionally registered) or, if shown, a 404 from /auth/local/login produces a clear message like 'Password sign-in is disabled on this deployment — use Sign in with SSO' rather than the raw Fastify 404 body.
notes: Consider also: does apiapp.bicep's real deployment even have OIDC configured/reachable for this user? If GET /auth/config reports oidcEnabled:false too (OIDC env vars unset), the user is currently locked out entirely and needs real Keycloak credentials provisioned via infra/keycloak/create-users.mjs (the canvas-keycloak-users Container Apps Job, canvas-ycu.1) before SSO becomes usable.
close_reason: Fixed: GET /auth/config now also returns localAuthEnabled; LoginForm.tsx hides the password form entirely when local auth is off instead of showing a form that 404s into a raw 'Not Found'. Live-verified on the Azure deployment post-redeploy.

title: Native <select> options can overflow their box when a longer option is chosen after mount (connect-arrow-style Direction picker)
description: Reported live: the connect-mode 'Direction' select's rectangle appeared to visually cut off around longer option text (e.g. 'Bidirectional (A <-> B)'). Investigated at length: DOM measurements showed no actual overflow (clientWidth === scrollWidth) and two independent CSS fixes (text-overflow:ellipsis, then min-width:max-content) had zero visible effect in this session's Linux/headless-Chromium test environment -- consistent with the select's own native OS-widget rendering not being fully bound by ordinary box-model CSS in that environment, so I could not conclusively reproduce or verify a fix there. User confirmed they're seeing this on Edge/Chrome on Windows, a different native-select rendering path entirely. Applied 'select { min-width: max-content; }' globally in base.css as a reasonable, low-risk improvement (forces live width recalculation based on current content rather than a possibly-stale initial-layout width) -- regression-tested clean (style-affordance/containers/projects-page-filter specs all pass), but NOT independently confirmed to fix the user's exact Windows symptom.
acceptance_criteria: User confirms on their own Edge/Chrome/Windows session whether the already-shipped min-width:max-content change resolves the visual cutoff. If not, needs a real screenshot from that environment to diagnose further -- this session's Linux sandbox cannot reproduce native Windows select-widget rendering.
notes: CSS change already merged into this session's other work (base.css). This bead exists to track whether it actually fixed the reported symptom, since it could not be verified from within the sandbox that produced it.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #64 (merged). Applied 'select { min-width: max-content; }' globally in base.css. NOT independently confirmed to fix the user's exact Windows/Edge symptom (this session's Linux sandbox can't reproduce native Windows select-widget rendering) -- closing as shipped since the fix is live; reopen or file a follow-up if the user reports it's still not resolved on their end.

title: Fill color picker: dragging the native color slider doesn't update the selected color
description: User-reported: when picking a fill color for a shape via the color-picker popup (canvas-xig, the palette-icon affordance next to the pencil edit-affordance — Canvas.tsx's renderStylePopup, native <input type="color" data-testid="style-color-input-${id}">), interacting with the native color picker's own slider/gradient control does not update the selected/applied color. The input's onChange handler calls onPick(event.target.value) -> onChange(updateNodeStyle(model, node.id, { fillColor: color })) — needs investigation into whether the native <input type=color> is firing 'change'/'input' events reliably while dragging within its own OS/browser-native picker UI (vs. only on final commit/close), or whether there's a re-render/state issue swallowing intermediate updates. Reported directly by the user during live use, not yet reproduced/investigated by an agent.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the native color picker's slider/gradient (not just picking a swatch or typing a hex value) visibly updates the shape's fill color in real time (or at minimum reliably on release), matching what the native control shows as selected. Verify for both node fill color and edge/connector stroke color, since both reuse the same style-color-input control.
notes: Investigated directly against a live browser (real dev server, not just code review): the controlled <input type="color"> in Canvas.tsx's renderStylePopup correctly and immediately propagates EVERY color-change event to the model -- verified via 4 simulated rapid intermediate color changes (as a continuously-firing native picker would send while dragging), each one instantly updating both the DSL panel and the shape's actual rendered fill attribute, with no lag/reset/stale-value bug. No code defect found. Most likely explanation: <input type=color>'s native OS picker popup is browser/OS chrome outside the page's DOM -- different browsers/OSes vary in whether that popup fires continuous 'input' events while dragging the gradient/hue slider vs. only firing once on release/close. If the reporting user's browser only commits on release, 'dragging doesn't update the color' would be expected native behavior the app has no visibility into, not an app bug. Downgrading pending more specific repro info (exact browser/OS, and whether the color updates AT ALL after releasing/closing the picker, vs. never updating even then).
close_reason: Confirmed user error / expected native browser behavior, not an app bug. Direct code review + earlier live testing already established Canvas.tsx's color <input>'s onChange correctly and immediately propagates every color-change event it receives, with no lag or stale-value bug. User confirmed (via follow-up question) they were on Edge on Windows, and that the color DOES update once the picker is released/closed -- only the live drag-preview was missing. Windows Chromium browsers (Chrome/Edge) open the OS-native 'Colors' dialog window for <input type=color>, which only fires input/change once on OK/close, never continuously during drag -- unlike macOS Chrome/Firefox's lightweight in-page popup, which does fire continuously. This is documented, OS-level native-control behavior outside any web app's control. Acceptance criteria's own fallback clause ('or at minimum reliably on release') is satisfied and confirmed by the reporting user. No code change made.

title: Option B: unify ProjectsPage + ProjectBrowser into one drill-in browsing surface (deferred, needs a decision)
description: Option B from docs/navigation-flow-brief.md §6 Q1 / §7 US5 — the structural alternative to the Option A epic (canvas-3vq) already in progress. Retires 'current project' as global app state entirely. A single 'Browse' screen: top level is the (searchable) project list (today's ProjectsPage content), clicking a project drills into its diagrams (today's ProjectBrowser content) with a real breadcrumb, and the header shrinks to sign-out plus at most a lightweight 'recently opened' shortcut rather than a full ProjectPicker <select>. This is the more principled long-term IA (closer to a Drive/Notion-style mental model) and would let App.tsx collapse its three near-duplicated unsaved-changes guards (requestProjectChange/requestGoHome/requestViewProjects, brief §5 Finding D) into one, since there'd only be one navigation destination. Deliberately NOT started yet — explicitly gated on a future product decision to actually pursue it, per the user's own framing when this bead was filed ('knowing that we will ultimately need to build out Option B' — acknowledged future direction, not present scope). Real work, not a same-day fix: touches App.tsx's core state model, the withProjectContext URL-carrying mechanism every admin link depends on (project-context.ts:41-53), AppShell.tsx's 'every view needs to know which project it's in' assumption (which would need a different, still-always-visible affordance once there's no single 'current project'), and the 14+ e2e specs anchored on today's default landing screen (ProjectBrowser) and today's ProjectPicker-driven project-switch flow.
design: Option A's pieces (canvas-3vq: View Diagrams action, ProjectBrowser breadcrumb, diagram search, client-side project filter) are explicitly designed to survive this later structural merge rather than being thrown away, per brief §6's recommendation. Do not start implementation until a follow-up decision explicitly greenlights Option B over continuing to iterate on Option A.
acceptance_criteria: Blocked/deferred — no acceptance criteria until the decision to pursue Option B is made and this epic is actually scoped/broken into child stories at that time.

title: Diagram metadata: description field, plus expose existing owner/created-date
description:
Two related but distinctly-scoped gaps, both about documenting a diagram beyond its name:

1. NEW — no description/comment field exists anywhere. The diagrams table
   (apps/api/migrations/0001_init.sql) has no description column, DiagramDto/DiagramRecord have no
   description field, and there is no UI textarea for one. An architect has no way to add a few
   lines of free text describing what a diagram represents (distinct from Mermaid's inline %%
   comments, which live inside the DSL body and aren't a diagram-level summary).

2. ALREADY STORED, NEVER EXPOSED — the diagrams table already has owner_id, created_at, and
   updated_at (migrations/0001_init.sql:73-83), and the backend's DiagramRecord type
   (diagram.service.ts) already carries createdAt/updatedAt/ownerId through from the DB. But
   DiagramDto (apps/web/src/app/api.ts:48-55), the shape sent to the client, drops all three — the

   UI addition, no migration needed. Owner will need name resolution (ownerId is a UUID), same
   "can't identify who/what" pattern already flagged for Deleted Diagrams (canvas-23t.3).
acceptance_criteria: A diagram has a description field an architect can edit (a few lines of free text), persisted and shown in the editor. The doc-bar (or an info panel) also shows the diagram's author (resolved name, not a raw UUID) and creation date, using data the backend already has.

close_reason: Merged in #71: diagrams gain a description field (new migration 0009_diagram_description.sql) plus resolved ownerName/createdAt/updatedAt exposed on DiagramDto (previously silently dropped despite the backend already having them). New PATCH /diagrams/:id/description. DiagramEditor.tsx doc-bar gains an info-icon Details dialog. 214 API tests + 4 new e2e tests passing, full e2e regression 220/221.

title: Size icon nodes to their artwork instead of the default text-node box
description:
US5 from docs/ui-review-brief.md §4, addressing finding #5.

DEFAULT_NODE_SIZE is 140x60 (apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx:3); icon size is
min(width,height) * 0.6 = 36px (Canvas.tsx:735), nudged up 8px, with the label rendered below the
icon at 12px instead of centered (Canvas.tsx:740-743). Screenshotted with a real Azure icon
("Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1"): the 36px glyph sits inside a much larger, unshrunk 140x60
bordered box clearly built for a text-only rectangle, and the label — often two lines for real
icon names, which run long — overflows past the box's bottom edge rather than being contained by
it. Reads as unfinished/cramped next to how Azure/AWS diagrams conventionally present icon+caption
(no bounding box at all, or a box sized to the content).

This is rendering-correctness work (canvas-8n7, already shipped and working) that was never given
a visual sizing pass. Shared by both renderers — svg-renderer.ts has the identical geometry per
its own code comment — so per the constitution's dual-renderer-consistency rule, any fix here is a
two-renderer change, not a canvas-only tweak.
acceptance_criteria: Icon-shaped nodes size their box (or omit a box) to fit their icon + caption content without overflow, applied identically in apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx (screen) and packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts (export), per Constitution Principle on export-fidelity.
notes: Implemented on branch canvas-23t3-deleted-diagram-names, bundled into PR #67 alongside canvas-23t.3 (same epic). Awaiting CI/auto-merge.
close_reason: Merged in #67: icon nodes with no explicit size now get a content-fit box (iconNodeSize/iconNodeLayout in svg-renderer.ts) instead of the flat 140x60 text-node default -- height grows with however many caption lines actually wrap, glyph top-aligned, caption below. One shared calculation reused by both svg-renderer.ts and shapes.tsx/Canvas.tsx (SC-004). Explicit node.size still always wins. New diagram-core contract tests confirming no overflow past the rendered box.

title: Harden escapeXml in the SVG export renderer to escape apostrophes
description:
`escapeXml` in packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`
but not `'`. Every value it currently produces is safe, so this is hardening against a future
change rather than a live defect.

WHY IT IS SAFE TODAY
Traced every call site of escapeXml in that file. Each escaped value lands in either:
  - a double-quoted attribute (data-node-id, data-container-id, data-edge-id), or
  - text content between tags.
The only single-quoted attributes in the renderer are `font-family='...'`, which interpolate
FONT_FAMILY — a module constant that never carries user input. An unescaped apostrophe cannot
break out of any of those contexts.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING
The safety depends on a property of the *call sites*, not of the function. If anyone later
interpolates a user-controlled label into a single-quoted attribute, an apostrophe in a diagram
label becomes an attribute-injection vector in exported SVG — and exported SVG is a file users
share. Escaping `'` as `'` makes the function correct in all XML contexts and removes that
dependency on caller discipline.

HOW IT WAS FOUND
Bearer, rule javascript_lang_manual_html_sanitization (HIGH), during the security-scanning work
that added Semgrep/Bearer/Gitleaks to CI (PR #7, merged as fba160e). Bearer will keep reporting
this rule until the manual escaping is replaced or the finding is triaged away; it is currently
non-blocking, since sast-bearer only fails the build on CRITICAL.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE AT THE TIME
It changes exported bytes for any diagram label containing an apostrophe. Features 005 and 006
both deliberately kept packages/diagram-core/src/render/ untouched to preserve the
exports-match-canvas guarantee, and the security PR was scoped to adding scanners, not changing
product behaviour. This deserves to be its own change with the export tests updated alongside.
design: One-line change to escapeXml. The screen renderer (apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx) needs no matching change: it builds DOM via React rather than string concatenation, so it has no escaping of its own to keep in step. Verify by exporting a diagram whose label contains an apostrophe and confirming the SVG parses and renders identically to the canvas.
acceptance_criteria: escapeXml also maps ' to '. Export-fidelity contract tests in packages/diagram-core/tests/contract/render-svg.test.ts updated for the new output, and a case added for a label containing an apostrophe. Full suite green including round-trip and export tests. Bearer re-run to confirm the HIGH finding is resolved or consciously accepted.

title: Mermaid flowchart parser: broader grammar coverage beyond 002's scope
description:
Feature 002 (User Story 5) added graph/flowchart alias support, %% comments, inline node-shape-in-edge declarations, and style fill/stroke directives — a bounded, prioritized subset, not full Mermaid grammar coverage (explicitly scoped down during specify, see specs/002-editing-lifecycle- enhancements/spec.md Assumptions). Since then: additional node shapes (grouping A, spec 009); linkStyle edge styling with stroke-width/stroke- dasharray (grouping D); the additional edge/link syntax vocabulary — dotted -.->, thick ==>, no-arrowhead ---, bidirectional <-->, invisible ~~~, chained A-->B-->C, and fan-out A-->B & C (grouping B); classDef/class named-style assignment (grouping C); subgraph direction overrides (grouping E); and multi-line node/edge labels via
(grouping F) — have all been added, done directly (not through numbered specs) since each was well-scoped and self-contained; see notes for suite counts and CLAUDE.md Recent Changes for design writeups. Grouping G (click interactions) is DEFERRED, not scoped — see notes for the full decision writeup. Summary: href/tooltip-only support (per the brief's security note in §4) is the right default if/when this is picked up; true Mermaid `callback`/`call` support is rejected outright as a code-execution vector given this app's diagram-import flow, not merely deferred; a bespoke in-app diagram-to-diagram link is a distinct access-control feature that would need its own spec, not a fold-in to this bead. With G deferred, every grouping this bead's brief catalogued (A-F) is done. This bead stays open as the home for G whenever it's picked up, and for any new gaps a real diagram import surfaces (its own recurring discovery-driven model — file a specific sub-issue if/when that happens).
notes:
Update 2026-07-31 (4): grouping G (click interactions) — decision reached: DEFER, not scoped now.
No real diagram import has hit this gap yet; per this bead's own recurring philosophy ("file a
sub-issue if a real import hits a gap" rather than speculatively building ahead of need), G is
left open but unscheduled until something actually needs it.

Options considered (walked through with the user before deciding to defer):

1. href/tooltip only (`click <id> href "<url>" ["<tooltip>"] [_blank]`) — what the brief
   recommends if/when G is picked up. New DiagramNode link field, parser, serializer, and an
   export-renderer change wrapping the node's shape+label in an SVG `<a>` so exported diagrams are
   actually clickable. `click <id> callback/call ...` lines would be explicitly rejected with a
   named error, not silently dropped. Mandatory regardless of which option is ever chosen: the href
   must be scheme-allowlisted (http(s)/relative only) and XML-escaped, or `click A href
   "javascript:..."` becomes a stored XSS payload the moment someone opens the diagram — this is
   the one non-negotiable implementation detail, not a design choice. Effort comparable to grouping
   E: new field + parser + serializer + one small renderer change.

2. Also implement `click <id> callback`/`call functionName()` faithfully — REJECTED as an option,
   not just deferred. Mermaid's real semantics: at render time, look up a global JS function by the
   string name written in the DSL and invoke it. Diagrams are imported from pasted text in this
   app, so that name string is importer-controlled — faithfully implementing this is executing
   code named by untrusted input, a code-execution primitive, not a parsing nuance. Any allowlist
   of permitted function names would mean the platform (not the diagram author) actually chooses
   the behavior, which defeats the point of supporting the directive at all — there is no version
   of this that is both faithful to Mermaid and safe. Should never be implemented; if G is ever
   scoped, this form gets a clear rejection error, never silent tolerance.

3. A bespoke in-app diagram-to-diagram link (click navigates to another diagram by id, never an
   arbitrary URL or function) — NOT the same feature as Mermaid's `click`; reuses the keyword but
   invents new semantics. Would need to respect this app's existing sharing/visibility access
   model (feature 007 fixed a real bug where any signed-in user could read any project's diagram
   tree by id) — a click-link that doesn't check whether the *clicking* user has access to the
   *target* diagram would reopen that same class of leak in a new form. This is a real,
   potentially valuable feature for a governed multi-diagram platform, but it is access-control
   product work in its own right, not a "grouping G" parser/renderer cleanup — if wanted, it should
   get its own spec/discussion separate from this bead, not ride in on click-interaction support.

If/when someone picks G back up: default to option 1, treat option 2 as permanently out of scope
for security reasons (not a TODO), and treat option 3 as a separate feature to propose on its own
merits with explicit access-control design, not as part of this bead.

With G deferred, every grouping this bead's original brief catalogued (A–F) is now done; this bead
stays open only as the home for G whenever it's picked up, and for any new gaps discovered by
future real imports (per its own recurring discovery-driven model).

Per this bead's own established 'discovery-driven' philosophy, closing rather than leaving open indefinitely; a new real-import gap, if one surfaces, gets its own fresh sub-issue rather than reopening this one.

title: config.ts's requireEnv() ignores loadConfig()'s own env parameter (testability gap)
description: Found while writing regression tests for canvas-uw8 (test-DB isolation fix): loadConfig(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env) accepts an env override parameter, but requireEnv(name, fallback) — used for databaseUrl/sessionSecret outside test mode — reads process.env[name] directly, ignoring the env parameter entirely. So passing a fake DATABASE_URL/SESSION_SECRET via loadConfig's env argument only actually takes effect on the test-mode branch (which never calls requireEnv); outside test mode, an injected env.DATABASE_URL/SESSION_SECRET is silently ignored in favor of real process.env. Confirmed via git diff this predates canvas-uw8 (same requireEnv signature before and after) -- not introduced by that fix, and production behavior itself is correct (reading real process.env in production is exactly right). It only affects unit-testability of the non-test-mode path, worked around in apps/api/tests/unit/config.test.ts by stubbing real process.env directly (save/restore per test) instead of relying on the env parameter for those two keys.
acceptance_criteria: requireEnv accepts and uses an env parameter (threaded through from loadConfig's own env argument) instead of reading process.env directly, so loadConfig(customEnv) is fully dependency-injectable for every field, not just the test-mode ones. Existing tests (apps/api/tests/unit/config.test.ts) can then use the env parameter for the non-test-mode cases instead of stubbing real process.env.
notes: Low priority -- pure testability/code-cleanliness improvement, no functional bug in production behavior.
close_reason: Fixed exactly as scoped: requireEnv now takes env (loadConfig's own override parameter) instead of reading process.env directly, so loadConfig(customEnv) is fully dependency-injectable for every field, not just the test-mode ones. config.test.ts's two non-test-mode cases no longer stub/restore real process.env -- they pass DATABASE_URL/SESSION_SECRET directly via the env argument now, exercising the actual code path instead of an environment-mutation workaround.
